articles.title: Shams Mulani spins India ‘A’ into 163-run lead against Australia ‘A’
articles.summary: Puducherry: Ravindra Jadeja and Manav Suthar are India’s top two left-arm finger spinners in Test cricket.
articles.body: Puducherry: Ravindra Jadeja and Manav Suthar are India’s top two left-arm finger spinners in Test cricket. But Shams Mulani showed at CAP-Siechem Stadium here on Wednesday that he can keep the duo on their toes.The Mumbai bowler’s four-wicket haul, which came after a 113 off 240 by wicketkeeper-batter Kumar Kushagra, helped India ‘A’ take a massive 163-run first-innings lead on a pitch that has quite a bit in it for the bowlers.India ‘A’ now have the option of enforcing a follow-on, with 150 being the mark in four-day matches, but the team management kept the Australians guessing about their decision until the third day morning.After India ‘A’ had put up 334, the seamers made good use of the wind and overcast conditions. Left-hander Campbell Kellaway was trapped LBW by Anshul Kamboj before Praful Hinge accounted for Nathan McSweeney, who was cleaned up by one that nipped away after pitching.Mulani (4-67) took over from there as he outfoxed captain Peter Handscomb with an arm ball that skidded through to crash into middle stump.Mulani varied his pace and sometimes looked to push the ball through, and still managed to get turn that kept the Australian batters on their toes.He got the wicket of right-hander Liam Scott (26) with one that sharply turned away and then removed danger-man Jason Sangha (46).Brief scores: India ‘A’ 334 (K Kushagra 113, T Kotian 69; C Rocchiccioli 4-95, T Murphy 3-77) vs Aus ‘A’ 171 (J Sangha 46; Shams Mulani 4-67).Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Puka Nacua Misses Another Rams Session as Injury Concerns Linger
articles.summary: Rams receiver Puka Nacua did not participate in the team's activities on Wednesday, putting his status up in the air for the game against the Broncos. The po...
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams receiver Puka Nacua did not participate in the team's jog-through on Wednesday, putting his status up in the air for Sunday Night's game against the Denver Broncos .

Nacua missed Monday Night against the New York Giants with a hip injury, which kept him out of multiple practices leading up to the game.

After a day off Tuesday, Rams head coach Sean McVay did not provide a definitive update on the pass-catcher, though he shared his approach to handling a player like Nacua.

"I think it's more along the lines of just seeing how that responds," McVay told the media.

"When you're a skill player and you're trying to hit high speed yards and open up… It's like some of the things that can almost be like pre-hernia is what he's feeling. You err on the side of caution."

Looking forward, Nacua's status will depend on when he reaches the point where time has allowed the injury and discomfort to heal.

"Usually, time is the best thing that allows that thing to heal. Then once you get to a certain point, I think you feel pretty good moving forward," McVay explained.

"But it's not something that, from talking with [Senior Vice President, Sports Medicine and Performance] Reggie [Scott] and our medical group, that we feel like is any sort of long-term threat.

"I just know that he's frustrated, and we all want him to be able to be out there, but we want him to be able to return to performance not just be able to gut through it."

With the season only two weeks old and the Rams' questionable handling of the Myles Garrett injury, the organization will understandably avoid a longer absence for Nacua and keep him upright.

The Rams will need Nacua against a tough Broncos defense, and their willingness to sit him will highlight just how notable his injury is.

articles.title: 'The night I could not sleep': Gautam Gambhir opens up on 'toughest decision' to drop Sanju Samson for Vaibhav Sooryavanshi
articles.summary: India head coach Gautam Gambhir has revealed the emotional difficulty behind one of his biggest selection calls in T20Is, admitting that dropping Sanju
articles.body: India head coach Gautam Gambhir has revealed the emotional difficulty behind one of his biggest selection calls in T20Is, admitting that dropping Sanju Samson during the England series left him unable to sleep.Samson, who was named Player of the Tournament during India's T20 World Cup triumph earlier this year, was left out after the first match of the five-game series in England in July. India had lost that opening T20I, with teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi coming into the XI for his T20I debut in Manchester.Gambhir said the decision weighed heavily on him, particularly because Samson had played such an important role in India's World Cup success. Speaking to JioStar ahead of India's home season against the West Indies, the India coach revealed just how difficult the call was."In two years of my journey, that was the only night I could not sleep and I told this to Sanju because I knew that it was probably the toughest decision in my coaching tenure in a T20 format because someone who was player of the tournament, and then you have to leave him out after three or four games. And the reason was probably Vaibhav was in that kind of form as well, and we had to win the series.“Because ultimately you are there and when you are playing for India, or when you are coaching India, you want to win each and every series possible. I had a very, very honest conversation with him and I told him that that is one of the reasons why, because Vaibhav was in that kind of form, and we needed someone to score runs at the top, we needed that little bit of a platform at the top as well. And he was fine with it. And that's a conversation which me and Sanju had, and he took it in good spirits," said Gambhir.The call was eventually reversed when India returned home for their three-match T20I series against Afghanistan. Samson came back into the side at Sooryavanshi's expense and went on to hit back-to-back fifties as India completed a 3-0 series sweep.Gambhir also used the episode to explain why even a player in exceptional form cannot automatically expect a place in India's playing XI."I know, it is (tough). But then, I made him understand that I know you're in good form, but sometimes with the players who have done well for a long time, you will have to wait for your opportunity.“There’s one more thing - social media or outside noise doesn't decide the playing eleven. Playing eleven who, in that dressing room, or who the coach and captain feel can win us the match, or what is the best playing eleven, and who have done well for such a long time because if Vaibhav plays today, then it's going to be a tough conversation between me and whoever we leave out, whether it's Abhishek or Sanju.“So we can't suddenly ignore that a combination that has created such an impact over the last one and a half or two years, that after three or four failures we drop them and play a young player who is very talented, who is also in very good form.“So sometimes you will have to wait for your opportunity and we still want to create that security in that dressing room. Because it is very easy for me to take popular decisions, but it is probably the toughest thing for me to take the right decisions and we've taken the right decision of continuing with Sanju and Abhishek," he explained.Sooryavanshi's emergence has nevertheless added another dimension to India's T20I selection puzzle. The teenager made his international debut in Manchester, but Gambhir stressed that India's established combination cannot be discarded simply because a young player is performing well.For the India coach, maintaining continuity remains particularly important given the team's recent success. Gambhir pointed to the short turnaround between India's World Cup triumphs while arguing against overreacting to isolated setbacks."For two years, imagine, you imagine we won the World Cup - which team in the history of sport has gone undefeated from one World Cup to the other and gone on to win the World Cup?“It didn't take these guys 17 years to win the second World Cup. It took these guys only 17 months to win the third World Cup. Suddenly one bad series or three bad games here and there does not make them a bad player or does not make us a bad side. So it was very important for us to have that continuity."Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Whatever is in the best interest of the team’: Gautam Gambhir’s candid Rohit Sharma admission
articles.summary: Gautam Gambhir's association with Rohit Sharma goes back much further than their time together in India's current coaching set-up.
articles.body: Gautam Gambhir's association with Rohit Sharma goes back much further than their time together in India's current coaching set-up.Long before Gambhir became India's head coach and Rohit led the national side, the two had already shared a dressing room. Gambhir was an established senior player when Rohit entered the India team, giving their relationship a familiarity that Gambhir believes made their later coach-captain equation different from a conventional one.Reflecting on the four India captains he has worked with during his coaching tenure in a conversation with JioStar, Gambhir explained that he and Rohit did not have to build their relationship from scratch when he became coach.“I don’t think so. See, Rohit’s and my relationship wasn’t just of captain and coach. Rohit’s and my relationship, when Rohit came into the team, I was a senior player at that time. So Rohit’s and my relationship is from back then. Rohit knew me since then. It is not like Rohit and I had a new relationship, or that I came as a coach from a foreign country who has neither seen Rohit play, nor knows Rohit individually or personally, what kind of person he is,” Gambhir said.That history meant Gambhir had already seen Rohit develop through different stages of his international career. Rohit, in turn, had known Gambhir as a senior India player well before Gambhir moved into the coaching role.According to Gambhir, that shared history can make it easier for a coach and captain to deal with situations where they do not necessarily arrive at the same conclusion.“So often when you have played together, things become very easy. And in fact, he knows my thinking, I know his thinking. Because tomorrow I might have some other thinking, the captain might have some other thinking, but ultimately, whatever is in the best interest of the team, if that’s the last final decision, then nothing can be better than that,” Gambhir said.For Gambhir, the key is therefore not that a coach and captain must always agree. Different views can exist, but an understanding of each other's thinking can help ensure those differences do not become a distraction when the final decision has to be made for the team.Rohit was the first of four India captains Gambhir has so far worked in his tenure. Suryakumar Yadav subsequently led the T20I side, while Shubman Gill and Shreyas Iyer have also taken on captaincy responsibilities.Despite the different leadership styles and personalities involved, Gambhir said he has found one common thread among all four captains.“And that’s why I said that with all four, whichever four captains I have worked with, this has been my experience with them, that everyone’s intention has been Indian cricket,” he said.Gambhir's comments come at a time when the narrative around Rohit has changed considerably following the Lord's ODI in July.Before that match, a media house had reported that the game could be the former India captain's last and that he had been told he was no longer part of the team's World Cup plans.Rohit then produced a commanding 138 in the match. BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia has subsequently spoken strongly in support of the veteran batter.There have also been developments around India's selection set-up. TimesofIndia.com earlier reported that Ajit Agarkar is less likely to receive an extension, with Parthiv Patel appearing to be the front runner for the chief selector's position.Against that backdrop, Gambhir's comments offer a glimpse into the long-standing understanding between two men whose professional relationship has evolved from senior player and young cricketer to captain and coach.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘You cannot go there half-cooked’: Gautam Gambhir’s message for Hardik Pandya ahead of 2027 WC
articles.summary: Hardik Pandya’s workload and lack of recent cricket could become a key consideration for India as they build towards the 2027 ODI World Cup, with head
articles.body: Hardik Pandya’s workload and lack of recent cricket could become a key consideration for India as they build towards the 2027 ODI World Cup, with head coach Gautam Gambhir stressing the all-rounder’s need for sufficient game time before the global tournament.India begin their World Cup preparations with the upcoming three-match ODI series against the West Indies, but will be without both Pandya and Jasprit Bumrah. Bumrah is away on Asian Games duty, while Pandya is still not fit to bowl 10 overs in an ODI.Gambhir, however, made it clear that both remain central to India’s plans for the World Cup in South Africa.“Whether it's Hardik, whether it's Jasprit Bumrah, both of them are going to be extremely important for us in South Africa. Because the way if you talk about Jassi or if you talk about Hardik, very few teams have a player like that who can bowl 10 overs for you, plus bat at number six or seven, plus with that impact,” Gambhir told JioStar ahead of India’s home season.The bigger concern for Pandya is match practice. After the IPL, the all-rounder has not played a substantial amount of cricket, and Gambhir believes that could leave him short of game time if his focus is primarily on the 50-over format.“Especially for Hardik, because he needs game time as well. Because after the IPL he hasn't played a lot of cricket. So if the focus is only that he has to play the 50-over format, then he might be short of cricket,” Gambhir said.For India, getting Pandya ready for the World Cup is not simply about his fitness. Gambhir wants him to enter the tournament with enough competitive cricket behind him to ensure his rhythm and confidence are in place.“Game time going into the World Cup is going to be extremely, extremely important. You cannot go there half-cooked. So you should have enough game time, your rhythm should be so good, because going to the World Cup, there are no ifs and buts,” he explained.The West Indies series will mark the beginning of India’s preparations for the 2027 World Cup, although Pandya and Bumrah will not be part of the opening phase. Their absence also comes at a time when India are managing an increasingly crowded international calendar.Gambhir indicated that workload management could become increasingly important, particularly when players have to move between formats in quick succession.India’s upcoming multi-format tour of New Zealand is a case in point. The first Test in Wellington begins on November 19, only three days after the fifth and final ODI against New Zealand in Tauranga. The tour features 12 matches across formats.Gambhir suggested that some senior batters could therefore be rested from portions of the ODI series to allow them to prepare properly for the two-Test assignment.“Often for Test match preparation, you will have to give your batters a break as well from white-ball to move into Test cricket, because coming from T20 to one-day cricket is easy,” he said.With only two days available for training before the Test series, players such as captain Shubman Gill, KL Rahul and Yashasvi Jaiswal could potentially benefit from a break from some ODIs, while Jasprit Bumrah, Mohammed Siraj, Ravindra Jadeja and Nitish Reddy could also face workload considerations.Gambhir believes the demands of modern international cricket will make three-format players increasingly difficult to maintain.“Look, ideally for any coach it is very important that as many players play all three formats, the better it is, because continuity in international cricket is very important,” he said.“So, as much as the coach wants, as much as the selectors want, whatever they do, you will have very few three-format players in the coming times, because you will have to keep rotating your players, whether they are spin bowlers or fast bowlers,” he explained.For Gambhir, however, Test cricket remains the foundation of a strong cricketing nation.“When you are getting the new guys in, obviously (you are) trying to make them feel how important Test cricket is, because I'm a very big believer that a strong Test cricketing nation is a strong cricketing nation.“It's not the other way around. I've never believed that a strong T20 cricket nation is a strong cricketing nation. So red-ball still remains our priority,” the coach asserted.Gambhir’s own tenure has already produced major white-ball success, with India winning the Champions Trophy and T20 World Cup during his two years in charge. The team, however, has also suffered Test-series defeats against New Zealand and South Africa at home.Reflecting on his tenure, Gambhir acknowledged that the journey has included both highs and lows.“I think I've had my own share of ups and downs, I think I've had my own failures and success. But again, I've always believed that when you take up that kind of a responsibility, there will always be ups and downs.”Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: After seven months away, Akash Deep's 'ubad-khabad' journey reaches comeback point | Exclusive Interview
articles.summary: Bengaluru: \"Chai ya coffee kuch lenge aap (Will you have tea or coffee?),\" says Akash Deep while adjusting his chair in the hotel lobby.
articles.body: Bengaluru: "Chai ya coffee kuch lenge aap (Will you have tea or coffee?)," says Akash Deep while adjusting his chair in the hotel lobby. "Saat mahine se cricket nahi khela ab finally khelunga(I have not played competitive cricket for the past seven months, now I will play)," he says, grinning from ear to ear before settling into a comfortable position.Akash Deep is happy, and there are multiple reasons. First, he has received the Right to Play (RTP) from the Centre of Excellence (CoE) and is ready to make a comeback after a long injury layoff. Second, he can't wait to check out of the hotel in Bengaluru, which has been his home for the past seven months.The 29-year-old has been included in the 15-member Rest of India squad, led by Rishabh Pant, which will take on 2025-26 Ranji Trophy champions Jammu and Kashmir in the Irani Cup match, starting from October 1 in Srinagar. The last time Akash Deep was in action was during the Ranji Trophy semifinal for Bengal, where they lost to the eventual champions, Jammu and Kashmir, by six wickets. It was during this match that Akash Deep suffered a lower-back stress fracture."I played that match with a 102 fever. It was my call and when it comes to playing for Bengal, I don't think twice. That state has given me so much. Whatever I am is because of Cricket Association Bengal (CAB). Even in the future, if I have to take a risk for Bengal to have a chance to win the Ranji Trophy, I will not think twice before taking it," says Akash.He smiles when asked about the risk of pushing himself at the end of the season, where he played every single game for the state across formats. The layoff turned out to be longer than he would have liked as it also ruled him out of the IPL 2026. Was it worth it?"Humare jaison ko har mauke pe khud ko saabit karna hota (For cricketers like us, we need to prove our credentials in every chance we get). It is easy to say, oh, I could have skipped that match... The workload was high, but it was a Ranji Trophy semifinal and there was a chance for us to lift that trophy. I know the injury gave a dent to my wallet as I missed out on the IPL, missed international cricket, but for me, I saw an opportunity where I had the chance to do something special on a bigger stage," he explains.The long layoff was frustrating but he chooses to focus on the brighter side and even during the difficult days, the opportunity to spend time with his family gave him happy memories. And the icing on the cake was sister's recovery from cancer."Spending weeks in the hotel rooms is not ideal. It is tough. But for me, these six months have been fruitful as well. My elder sister recovered from cancer. I got married, got appointed as Deputy Superintendent of Police by the Bihar government and, most importantly, got married," he laughs.Behind all the giggles, laughter and excitement of making a comeback lies a painful chapter in Akash's life. He has endured rejection, contemplated quitting cricket, lost his father and elder brother, searched for an oxygen cylinder for his mother during the Covid-19 pandemic and even learned to drive a truck to make ends meet.Yet, when he speaks about the darkest phase of his life, it is none of these moments that he recalls. His sister Akhand Jyoti Singh's cancer diagnosis broke him.There was a time I thought of quitting cricket. She kept me going and when she was diagnosed with cancer, I was shattered"She was the one who had forced me to pursue cricket. There was a time I thought of quitting cricket. She kept me going and when she was diagnosed with cancer, I was shattered. I was pleading with God, please not her. I have lost my father, my brother, how much more will God take from me? What would I do with all the money and fame if I won't have people to enjoy those with?" he says."Luckily, I was playing for Lucknow Super Giants (LSG) in the IPL. Every day, after completing the training, I used to rush to the hospital and come back around 2:30 am, and on the match day, I used to go to the hospital straight after the match and come back in the morning. I was not eating properly. I was not training properly. I had no focus on my cricket. Then there were travels in the IPL. I was scared that I might lose her," he adds.Post IPL, Akash Deep went to England, where his heroics at Edgbaston helped India win the Test. "She was going through chemotherapy. I was again all over the place. She told me to play for her and that's why I dedicated my match-winning performance to her," he recollects.Recovery from injuryAkash praises the BCCI's Centre of Excellence (CoE) for helping him regain complete match fitness. The crafty seamer dismissed the criticism surrounding the CoE and its injury management."I am here for so many months now and I never faced any issue. There was a clear plan given to me and I have recovered following the instructions given by the CoE. It is a world-class facility. I have played cricket in other countries as well, but I must say when it comes to infrastructure, CoE is way ahead," he says."Aap mujhe ek baat batao, agar aapne sharaab pi kar apni liver kharab kar li hai toh kya usme doctor responsible hai (Let me ask you something: if you have damaged your liver by drinking alcohol, is the doctor responsible for that?). We should have a CoE-like facility in every state of India," he adds.Fit again, Akash knows the road won't be easy for him. He will have to toil again to regain his place in the Indian team. There is pressure, but his body's readiness and the excitement to regain his spot give him the feeling of a kid in a candy shop."I will have to perform well in the Irani Trophy first. Then, if picked, I need to do well for India A. Yes, I want to make a comeback in the Indian team and it won't be that easy. But I am ready for the grind," he says.Over the years, Akash has navigated trials, tribulations, fame and accolades, his journey has been as unpredictable as the road he grew up near. He describes it in his own words: "Apne gaon ki sadak jaisi journey rahi hai bilkul, ubad-khabad" (My journey has been like the road in my village, topsy-turvy).He hails from Sasaram, a place steeped in history, where Afghan ruler Sher Shah Suri defeated Mughal emperor Humayun at the Battle of Chausa in 1539. It was during Sher Shah Suri's reign that the Grand Trunk Road, also known as the Sher Shah Suri Road, was built. And perhaps there is something fitting about that: Akash Deep's journey, much like the GT Road that runs through India, has been rough, winding and uneven, but it has carried him a long way.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi to replace Tilak Varma or Shivam Dube in ‘six months’, predicts ex-India cricketer
articles.summary: Mohammad Kaif believes India could face a major selection headache in the T20I format within the next six months, with the former batter predicting that
articles.body: Mohammad Kaif believes India could face a major selection headache in the T20I format within the next six months, with the former batter predicting that Vaibhav Sooryavanshi will force his way into the first-choice side.Kaif feels the teenage sensation’s emergence could eventually leave either Tilak Varma or Shivam Dube fighting for a place in the playing XI, despite Tilak currently being India’s vice-captain.“I understand that Tilak is the vice-captain. But vice-captains have also been dropped before. I do not want to go there. Shivam Dube is not scoring in every game and still has to prove himself. Fielding is also his weakness, and he is not a proper bowling all-rounder. He is only playing as a batter. After six months, either Tilak or Dube will be out. You will have to remove one, and Sooryavanshi will play. I am saying this right now", Kaif said on his YouTube channel.Kaif pointed to Sooryavanshi’s performances beyond T20Is as another reason for his prediction. The teenager also made an impact in the Duleep Trophy and even bowled during the tournament, adding another dimension to his game.“Sooryavanshi scored in the Duleep Trophy as well. He has improved his game. He was even bowling there. So he has understood that if he can bowl a few overs, he will have an advantage,” he added.The numbers behind Sooryavanshi’s rapid rise are difficult to overlook. In his first six T20Is of 2026, he has scored 193 runs at an average of 32.17 and a strike rate of 189.22. He has found the boundary once every 3.4 deliveries and hit a six every 7.2 balls.His IPL campaign strengthened that case further. Sooryavanshi finished the season with 776 runs at an average of 48.50 and a strike rate of 237.51, including 72 sixes.Those numbers have already shifted the conversation around the teenager. Rather than being viewed solely as a young player being gradually introduced to international cricket, Sooryavanshi is increasingly making a case for a regular place in India’s T20I setup.Tilak’s numbers, meanwhile, remain respectable on the surface. He has scored 395 runs in T20Is in 2026 at an average of 35.91 and a strike rate of 154.90.However, the timing of some of those runs adds another layer to the debate. His fifty came in the fifth and final T20I against England, by which point India had already lost the series, and India went on to lose that match as well.Another notable contribution came during the Zimbabwe tour, although the quality of the opposition bowling was not necessarily of the highest pedigree.There have also been occasions when Tilak has found it difficult to rotate the strike after being promoted up the order or arriving at the crease earlier than expected, particularly against spin. At the other end of the innings, however, he has shown greater effectiveness as a finisher, including against Jofra Archer.That creates a contrast in the type of batter India could eventually have to choose between. Sooryavanshi represents an extreme-tempo approach built around relentless boundary-hitting, while Tilak offers greater adaptability and the ability to construct an innings.Dube’s numbers also make the selection debate more complicated than Kaif’s assessment might suggest.The all-rounder has scored 415 T20I runs in 2026 at an average of 31.92 and a strike rate of 170.78. At the T20 World Cup, he scored 235 runs at a strike rate of 169.06, giving India substantial returns from a player primarily selected for his power-hitting.The more pertinent question surrounding Dube is his bowling contribution.He has bowled only 26 overs across 23 T20Is in 2026, taking 12 wickets while conceding 12.44 runs per over. Those figures underline how India have largely used him as a batter who can provide occasional overs rather than as a genuine bowling all-rounder.That distinction could become important if Sooryavanshi continues to add bowling to his skill set.For now, India have a number of options in their T20I batting group. But Kaif’s six-month prediction has put the spotlight firmly on a question that could become increasingly difficult for the selectors to avoid: how long can a player with Sooryavanshi’s scoring numbers remain outside the first-choice XI?Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Leicestershire: Foxes to appeal against 27-point ECB penalty
articles.summary: Leicestershire are to appeal against the 27-point ECB penalty they received for breaching pitch regulations in August.
articles.body:
Leicestershire are to appeal against the decision to deduct them 27 points for the pitch they prepared for the County Championship Division One match against Glamorgan in August.

The penalty imposed by the independent Cricket Discipline Panel midway through their penultimate match of the season consisted of a £5,000 fine, the loss of all 19 points earned in the win over Glamorgan and an extra eight-point penalty, which dropped them to the bottom of the table.

They were given 10 days to decide whether to appeal - and chief executive Emma White has now confirmed they will do that, on the morning of their final Championship game of 2026, away to title-chasing Warwickshire.

"The club respects the Cricket Discipline Panel (CDP) process, which is ongoing," she said in a statement.

"However, we have serious concerns about the process that resulted in the panel's decision on the charge and the sanctioning procedure. I can confirm that the club will be appealing.

"The club has instructed specialist sports law barrister Craig Harris of Furnival Chambers to advise and represent us, and Oliver Laurence of Periculum Sport to provide independent expert and strategic support throughout the appeal.

"The panel itself found that the club did not intend the pitch to play as it did and that this was not a case of cheating. Our grounds team has an outstanding record, and I am proud of the work they do.

"As we intend to appeal, it would not be appropriate for the club to comment further at this stage.

"I would ask all supporters to do the same, and to treat everyone involved, including players and staff from other counties, and those involved with administering this process, with courtesy and respect, both at the ground and online."

It means that the Championship will conclude this Sunday with uncertainty over which two clubs will drop into Division Two for 2027.

Hampshire are already relegated - but the Foxes' fate may also impact Surrey, who visit another of three title-chasing sides Somerset, as well as Essex and Glamorgan, who meet in Cardiff.

Leics 'spurred on' by points penalty - Thomas

Leics on brink of relegation after points deduction

Following the Foxes' 42-run win against Glamorgan, only their second Championship victory of the season, the pitch was rated as "poor" in match referee Ian Ramage's report.

Glamorgan head coach Richard Dawson said batting conditions had been "tough", although there were 774 runs in the match, which lasted all four scheduled days .

Referee Ramage asked for the ECB's pitch and grounds advisor Andy Mackay to carry out a post-match inspection.

The starting point for punishment for a pitch rated as "poor" is a 16-point deduction.

This was reduced to eight points at the tribunal because of several mitigating factors.

Among them were Leicestershire's "early admission that the pitch was substandard" and this being the "first rating of below average, poor or unfit" in the previous 24 months.

In his interview with the Cricket Regulator before the tribunal hearing, Leicestershire head groundsman Callum Lewin said there were "circumstances leading up to the game that were just out of my control".

They included an "unscheduled Bollywood filming event" taking place at the Foxes' Uptonsteel Grace Road home four days before the start of the match.

The exceptionally hot weather was also a reason for the pitch being dry.

A further eight-point deduction has been suspended for a year.

The Foxes have faced a summer-long battle to avoid the drop in their first summer back in Division One after a 22-year exile, having won their first promotion as Division Two title winners last September.

articles.title: County Championship: Leicestershire appeal 27-point deduction for poor pitch blamed on Bollywood film shoot
articles.summary: Leicestershire chief executive Emma White has confirmed the club will be appealing its 27-point deduction for the poor pitch that groundsman Callum Lewis later argued was due to a Bollywood film shoot;
articles.body:
Leicestershire's groundsman Callum Lewin had argued filming of an unscheduled Bollywood film - believed to be for a biopic of former India captain Sourav Ganguly - had taken place at the ground four days before the Glamorgan fixture, preventing the pitch from being covered for eight hours in bright sunshine.

This was dismissed by the panel as a mitigating factor as it was only one day.

"The club respects the Cricket Discipline Panel process, which is ongoing. However, we have serious concerns about the process that resulted in the Panel's decision on the charge and the sanctioning procedure," said Leicestershire chief executive Emma White.

"I can confirm that the club will be appealing."

The independent Cricket Discipline Panel (CDP) upheld the Cricket Regulator's charge against Leicestershire for breaching the ECB Pitch Regulations, with the pitch at Uptonsteel Grace Road rated as 'poor' during the County Championship match against Glamorgan, between August 20-23.

Leicestershire won the low-scoring match by 42 runs and the pitch was inspected immediately after.

The statement added that Leicestershire have instructed sports law barrister Craig Harris of Furnival Chambers to advise and represent the club.

"The Panel itself found that the club did not intend the pitch to play as it did and that this was not a case of cheating. Our grounds team has an outstanding record, and I am proud of the work they do," White added.

"As we intend to appeal, it would not be appropriate for the club to comment further at this stage. I would ask all supporters to do the same, and to treat everyone involved, including players and staff from other counties, and those involved with administering this process, with courtesy and respect, both at the ground and online."

In a full written judgment, match referee Ian Ramage logged 43 examples of uneven bounce in the match. The pitch had an unusual look, with a green middle (16mm of grass) to help seamers and bare ends (just 3mm) to help spinners. Other pitches at Grace Road this year have had a similar look and played differently.

The Regulator acknowledged Leicestershire would not have deliberately created a pitch to bounce so unevenly but stated "each of these factors presented foreseeable risks that should have informed part of the planning and preparation process".

In conclusion, the tribunal found that, while Leicestershire did not intend for the pitch to play unevenly, their approach to preparing it was unreasonable.

"Accordingly, and for these reasons, LCCC have failed to discharge the burden upon them under Regulation 7.6 that it "sought, acting reasonably, to prepare the best quality pitch that it could for the match that was being staged."

Leicestershire recently kept their Division One survival hopes alive with a five-wicket win over Hampshire.

articles.title: Jos Buttler injury derails England as Sri Lanka seal 16-run win in second ODI to level series
articles.summary: Jos Buttler suffered a hamstring injury but returned 10 overs later and limped to the field; Sri Lanka managed to peg England back after a strong start to their chase; watch the third and final ODI live on Sunday from 10am live on Sky Sports Cricket (first ball 10.30am)
articles.body:
It was a match filled with drama encapsulated by Jos Buttler's innings. Buttler looked like he was going to be the match-winner but in the 38th over, he had to retire hurt after pulling up with England on 254-4 due to what appeared to be a hamstring injury.

Buttler limped back out in the 48th over but could add only two more runs before being dismissed. Will Jacks (52), Rehan Ahmed (0), Gus Atkinson (16) and Jamie Overton (2) also fell as England's chase floundered, with just one four and one six coming from the 37th over onwards.

It was a remarkable comeback from Sri Lanka after Ben Duckett (67) and Tom Banton (73) had given England an incredibly strong start, but inspired bowling from Dunith Wellalage (3-49) proved decisive, alongside a sensational 121 from Sri Lanka captain Kusal Mendis.

The series will now be decided on Sunday September 27 at The Kia Oval, with first ball at 10.30am, live on Sky Sports .

A tale of two spells: Sri Lanka start badly and end exceptionally

When Sri Lanka set England a target of 322, the hosts would have been optimistic about chasing it down - even more so after Banton and Duckett made a blistering start, with Asitha Fernando (1-68) and Dilshan Madushanka (2-54) struggling for line and length.

England raced past 50 inside six overs and reached 82-0 after 10, needing 240 more for victory. It was their highest-ever ODI Powerplay score against Sri Lanka.

More milestones quickly followed, with Duckett bringing up his 10th ODI fifty in the 12th over before Banton reached his second in the 15th. The latter continued to canter towards a career-best score with England firmly in control.

Sri Lanka finally found the breakthroughs they needed through Wellalage, who single-handedly began to derail England's chase. His deceptive delivery accounted for Duckett for 67 before he caught Banton out of his crease.

Wellalage struck again when England captain Harry Brook (1) was trapped lbw two overs later, with Sri Lanka successfully reviewing the original decision. England were suddenly 157-3 and still needed 165.

Sachindu Colombage (1-55) then claimed the prized wicket of Joe Root (17). Although England passed 200, they still had plenty of work to do with 21 overs remaining.

Buttler looked like he could be the difference when he came to the crease, attacking from the outset and bringing up his 46th ODI half-century from just 36 balls.

But England's chase was derailed when Buttler suffered a hamstring injury while running between the wickets and had to retire hurt.

Jacks attempted to steady the innings and reached his half-century, but Sri Lanka steadily turned the screw, restricting the scoring rate before Ahmed, Atkinson and Overton all fell as the visitors' death bowling took control.

Buttler limped back out in a final attempt to rescue England, but could add only two more runs before Kamindu Mendis took the catch that dismissed him for a second time at the start of the 50th over.

That left Jofra Archer (0no) and Josh Tongue (1no) needing 19 from the final over. Only three runs came from it as Sri Lanka secured a victory full of character.

Kusal Mendis stars with sensational captain's knock

After winning the toss and electing to bat on a strong Headingley surface, Sri Lanka made a steady start. Pathum Nissanka (25) fell to the final ball of the ninth over, but the visitors still reached 46-1 at the end of the Powerplay.

From there, Kamindu Mendis (54) and captain Kusal Mendis (121) built an outstanding partnership. They took Sri Lanka past 100 in the 20th over before the boundaries began to flow.

Mendis brought up his half-century in the 23rd over and celebrated with a huge six. Kamindu then reached his fourth ODI fifty from 56 balls, with England's spin options Ahmed (2-48) and Jacks (0-33), as well as Tongue (0-55), coming under pressure.

England eventually got the breakthrough they needed in the 30th over when Brook caught Kamindu on the boundary.

Mendis continued to build despite losing his partner and brought up his century from just 82 balls in the 31st over, striking a four. His wicket had been preserved by a successful review on the previous delivery after he was initially given out caught behind, with UltraEdge showing no contact.

It was the Sri Lanka captain's seventh ODI century, featuring 12 fours and three sixes. It also made Atkinson's costly drop in the 15th over, when Mendis was only 17, even more significant.

Kusal Mendis eventually fell in the 36th over attempting another boundary, finding Banton in the deep to leave Sri Lanka 222-3.

Charith Asalanka (11), Pavan Rathnayake (47), Janith Liyanage (32), Wellalage (16no) and Sachindu Colombage (3no) all chipped in during the closing overs to push Sri Lanka to 321-5 - a total that proved just enough to level the series.

'Nothing special' - Kusal salutes Sri Lanka for doing the basics

Sri Lanka captain and player of the match Kusal Mendis (121 off 100 balls)…

"I'm so happy winning and getting the hundred. The overall performance was very good.

"We started really well and the middle order batted really well. Nothing special, basic cricket and I was very happy with 320, we wanted more than 300 on this pitch.

"Wellalage bowled really well, the whole team, after the powerplay. The guys gave 100 per cent.

"Today is finished and now we have to focus on the next game and do the basics right."

"It was an outstanding game. You can look back and dwell on some many different areas but that is not what this team does, we go back to the drawing board and get ready for The Oval.

"We put up a really good fight with the ball. To restrict them to 320 and have the chance to chase that down was a hell of an effort.

"The lads got the chase off to a flyer. You couldn't really ask for much more. We probably stalled in that middle period and lost a few too many wickets, but the fight we showed was great.

"We've got a great opportunity now to try and win this series, and a great opportunity for 12 months' time. In pressure situations, like the one that awaits us at The Oval, it will be great to see where we are as a team."

articles.title: Father’s 'affairs', property fear: Why Kanpur millionaire’s son ordered the hit job
articles.summary: LUCKNOW: The son of a pharmaceutical trader allegedly conspired to kill his father fearing that the 60-year-old man, who had relationships with several
articles.body: LUCKNOW: The son of a pharmaceutical trader allegedly conspired to kill his father fearing that the 60-year-old man, who had relationships with several women, might end up transferring his property to another woman, police said Thursday, days after arresting the victim's daughter-in-law and two alleged contract killers in the case.Vineet Manocha (60), who ran a pharmaceutical firm on Birhana Road with his son, was stabbed to death at his Ratan Orbit apartment in Kalyanpur in Kanpur on September 5.His son Subrat Manocha was arrested on Wednesday night and sent to judicial custody on Thursday. He was subsequently taken to jail, police said.Police had arrested Vineet's daughter-in-law Shalu Manocha and alleged contract killers Vishal and Rajkishore the day after the murder.The arrest of Subrat has also opened the possibility of Shalu being released from the case, with police saying she has not been given a clean chit yet but that a report could be submitted before the court if sufficient evidence is not found against her.Commissioner of police Raghubir Lal told news agency PTI that the conspiracy came to light through analysis of call detail records (CDRs), CCTV footage, digital and scientific evidence, recoveries and other circumstantial evidence.Deputy commissioner of police (West) SM Qasim Abidi said Subrat had accumulated debts of more than Rs 40 lakh through gambling and IPL betting.According to police, Subrat's father gave him around Rs 40,000 every month for his expenses, while he was paying about Rs 55,000 a month towards loan instalments.During interrogation, Subrat told police that his father had relationships with several women and feared that he would start living with another woman and transfer all his property in her name. So, he hatched the plan to kill him.The police said the initial plan was to make Vineet's death appear accidental or natural, but the plan was later changed.Police also found deleted chats between Subrat and Vishal and said their locations had coincided at several points before the murder.These findings prompted police to revisit the allegations against Shalu, who was arrested along with Vishal and Rajkishore during the initial investigation.Lal said the subsequent probe had so far not found sufficient corroborating evidence establishing Shalu's involvement.Police also alleged that Subrat and Vishal had attempted to divert suspicion towards Shalu."All scientific, digital, CDR, CCTV and circumstantial evidence will be independently verified and scrutinised," Lal said, adding that if Shalu's involvement was not established after a proper investigation, police would submit a report before the court.According to Lal, Vishal told investigators that Subrat had asked him to kill his father and allegedly promised him Rs 6 lakh. Vishal also allegedly claimed that Subrat had instructed him to name Shalu if he was caught.Police are verifying Vishal's allegations against call records and other digital and circumstantial evidence. Lal said Subrat had not confessed to the murder.Police also found that Vishal had obtained a new SIM card a couple of days before the murder and made his first call from the number to Subrat, Lal said.Police questioned Subrat, Shalu and Vishal in several rounds on Wednesday night.During one confrontation, Shalu allegedly broke down and told police that she had been implicated to protect Subrat.Subrat, who had remained under suspicion during the investigation, was detained and questioned extensively before his arrest.Police said investigators had prepared more than 100 questions and were examining the accused over their movements, phone calls, financial transactions and other links surrounding the murder.During the remand, police also took Vishal to Ratan Orbit, where he allegedly threw a key while fleeing after the murder. The key was subsequently recovered from an empty plot adjoining the apartment complex, police said.Rajkishore was taken to Kanpur Central railway station, where police claimed to have recovered his blood-stained trousers and a black scarf from behind a public toilet on his pointing-out.Lal said Shalu, Vishal and Rajkishore were sent back to jail after undergoing a medical examination around 11am on Thursday, about an hour before their 24-hour police custody remand ended.He stressed that Shalu had not yet been given a clean chit.The 24-hour custody remand of the three accused ended at noon on Thursday, after which they were scheduled to be taken back to jail following the medical examination, PTI reported.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kanpur | Silver Rate in Kanpur | Bank Holidays in Kanpur | Public Holidays in Kanpur | Kanpur AQI | Weather in Kanpur | Petrol Price in Kanpur | Diesel Price in Kanpur | CNG Price in Kanpur | LPG Price in KanpurStay updated with the latest Kanpur news. articles.title: County Championship: Leicestershire relegated by Warwickshire, subject to appeal
articles.summary: Leicestershire are relegated, subject to an appeal against their points deduction, after being bowled out cheaply by title-chasing Warwickshire.
articles.body:
Rothesay County Championship, Division One, Edgbaston (day one)

Leicestershire 125: Cox 33; Bamber 4-42, Woakes 3-20

Warwickshire 130-4: Hain 37*; Holland 2-29

Warwickshire (3 pts) lead Leicestershire (1 pt) by five runs

Warwickshire's march towards a ninth County Championship title continued apace at Edgbaston as relegation-bound Leicestershire became the latest to be crushed by the Bears' irrepressible bowling attack.

The visitors chose to bat in a bid to earn batting points essential to their survival hopes - but that plan went spectacularly pear-shaped as they succumbed for 125 to effectively confirm their demotion, subject to appeal.

Only Ben Cox (33) and Sol Budinger (27) resisted for long against a bang-in-form attack led by Ethan Bamber (4-42) and Chris Woakes (3-20).

The hosts then reached 130-4 by the close, with Sam Hain on 37, within reach of 1,000 runs for the season.

Leicestershire to appeal against 27-point penalty

Leicestershire's strange decision to bat first suited Warwickshire's plan perfectly and their rampant attack - who had bowled out the opposition for less than 200 seven times out of nine - maintained that streak.

They took two wickets in the first two overs as Sheridon Gumbs played inside Bamber's fourth ball which hit off-stump and Rishi Patel offered no shot to be LBW to Woakes, who then Steve Eskinazi caught at point.

With the Foxes 15-3, overseas linchpin Nick Kelly having returned home injured and Hamza Shaikh unable to play against the club from which he is still technically on loan, Leicestershire were in disarray.

They never recovered as Jonny Tattersall and Budinger and fell to successive deliveries.

Tattersall became Olly Hannon-Dalby's 370th first-class wicket for Warwickshire before Budinger edged the next ball, from skipper Ed Barnard, to second slip.

Former Worcestershire keeper Ben Cox, a T20 Finals Day winner on this ground eight years ago, and skipper Ian Holland dug in either side of lunch.

But Bamber struck twice more as Holland edged to third slip and Ben Green nicked to first.

A perfect outswinger from Woakes ended Cox's diligent innings, Ajaz Patel dragged on a pull at Bamber and Josh Hull then offered a simple return catch.

Warwickshire's reply started badly when Rob Yates played on to Holland's seventh ball.

Dan Mousley struck four quick fours to get the innings going but then changed his bat and edged the next ball, from Holland, to third slip.

Will Young edged Green to first slip and Vansh Jani started with two sparkling boundaries but then skied a mow at spinner Patel, but Hain once again delivered the vital central role.

As composed and organised as ever, accompanied by a flurry of boundaries from Barnard, it was a five off the helmet that eased the Bears in front just before the close.

articles.title: County Championship: England's Emilio Gay hits fine 141 for Durham against Lancashire
articles.summary: England opener Emilio Gay scores a stylish 141 for Durham, who end day one of their Division Two match against Lancashire on 355-5.
articles.body:
Rothesay County Championship, Division Two, Old Trafford (day one)

Durham 355-5: Gay 141, McKinney 71, Agarwal 66; Bailey 2-52

England opener Emilio Gay made 141 as Durham dominated the first day of their County Championship match against Lancashire, with the visitors ending on 355-5.

Gay's high-class century at Emirates Old Trafford was his fourth in 10 Championship innings this season and it helped his side make good on their pledge not to take it easy even though the Division Two title is won.

Gay put on 114 with Ben McKinney, who made 71 and reached 1,000 first-class runs for the season in the process. He then added 168 with Mayank Agarwal before being caught at a precisely placed second slip off Ben Walkden when his side were eight runs short of a second batting point.

A tough few hours for Lancashire's bowlers was eased a little when they took three wickets in the evening session, though it is doubtful whether this will assuage the pain of dropping four catches, all off Durham's highest scorers.

Pick your County Championship team of the season

The shape of the day was already clear by lunch, when the visitors were 112-1 with McKinney unbeaten on 64.

Alex Lees was caught behind off Tom Bailey for three in the third over of the morning but McKinney and Gay had put on an unbroken 102 by the first interval, hitting 17 boundary fours on a pitch that justified Lees' decision to bat first.

The afternoon began badly for Durham when McKinney, who had given two tough chances before he reached 50, played a horrendous flat-footed drive to a ball from Bailey and was caught behind by Matty Hurst for 71.

That wicket fell in the fourth over of the session and ended a 114-run stand for the second wicket but, as was the case in the morning's play, an early wicket was a prelude to Durham's domination.

Gay was joined by India's Agarwal, who announced himself by pulling Mitch Stanley for a four and a six off successive balls. Gay reached his century off 156 balls when he stroked through midwicket for his 14th boundary four.

Agarwal brought up his fifty off 101 balls just before tea by which time Durham were 247-2 and the third-wicket pair had nearly doubled the score and put on 123.

The batters continued to bat serenely in the evening session and it was a surprise when Gay guided Walkden straight to Harris. But that wicket began a fine spell for Lancashire, whose left-arm spinner, Noman Ali, took the next two wickets.

Umpire Hassan Adnan judged that Colin Ackermann had edged a catch to Hurst on six but there was no doubt about the one to Josh Bohannon at cover that meant the departure of Agarwal for 66.

Those wickets left Durham on 306-5 but Ollie Robinson and Kasey Aldridge had steered their side to a third bonus point at the close. Noman finished the day with figures of 2-110.

articles.title: Mark Wood retires: England bowler's best spells in his own words
articles.summary: As England bowler Mark Wood retires from international cricket, he talks through his most famous spells from his Test career.
articles.body:
When Mark Wood retired on Tuesday, he brought to an end one of the most entertaining England careers in recent years.

The fastest England bowler on record by most metrics, he produced a number of thrilling spells in a career too often hit by injuries.

Here are four of those spells in his own words...

'That was the fastest' - the Saint Lucia breakthrough

Despite bowling quickly on occasions, Wood averaged 41.73 with the ball across his first 12 Tests. Then, on the advice of West Indies legend Michael Holding, he lengthened his run-up and using it for the first time, took 5-41 in the first innings of the third Test against West Indies in Saint Lucia in 2019.

"That was the fastest. I could be biased because I thought it was a breakthrough moment in my career but when I was watching the ball carry off the nicks, they felt a long way in the slips.

"You feel weightless, like you're never tired and are just picking up speed. It feels like you have all of this momentum and loose energy to release. You feel a surge through your body and then a whip out of your fingers.

"That day I didn't have to try. Root could have put the field anywhere and I wouldn't have cared. I was so up in my action. I can remember my feet landing and the feeling of the balls on my fingers - the seam ripping up my fingers.

"I essentially had two different careers – the first one in and out of the team with good moments but struggling with ankle injuries and form. I felt I had to constantly push myself with that stop-start run-up to get the most out of myself.

"As soon as I went off my longer run I had much more momentum, flow and freedom and the ability to bowl consistently quicker for longer.

"When I lengthened my run-up, if it was below 90mph I was annoyed."

Wood's best match figures are 9-100 from the fourth Test against South Africa in Johannesburg in 2020. On a quick and bouncy pitch, Wood averaged 89.1mph and helped England secure a 191-win run.

"I faced [South Africa bowler] Anrich Nortje there and when he bowled a bouncer I could hear it go past me. I was honestly so scared but something clicked in me that I would bowl fast.

"I got Rassie van der Dussen for 98 caught from round the wicket. We double-bluffed him. That was a great wicket because he was giving us a bit of verbals back.

"Faf du Plessis wasn't happy with something and Van der Dussen got involved.

"The way he commands a presence at the crease winds people up and he has a little bit of verbals here and there.

"A few of the lads were desperate for me to stick one up him.

"We set up this bouncer plan, I pitched it up and he hit it straight to cover."

Wood's best innings figures came at the end of the 2021-22 Ashes defeat when he took 6-37 in the second innings of the final Test in Hobart.

"It is disappointing because you are losing but you still have the pride in your own performance. You have to have pride in your performance.

"I wanted to do it for Spoons [coach Chris Silverwood]. He was under a lot of pressure but was really good for me and backed me up - Jon Lewis the bowling coach as well.

"I played four out of the five Tests and was proud of that. I was so tired at the end of that spell but came out with my best figures of the tour.

"[The Australian public] respected that I kept trying and bowling quickly. Even on the boundary line the Australia fans were saying 'Woody, we want to see you on'.

"[Afterwards] I was in the lift with Justin Langer and he put his hand up and pulled me in and said 'respect'.

"That was a really nice moment. We always want respect from our people but to have it from the Australians was nice."

Wood will likely be best remembered for his devastating 5-34 in the first innings of the third Ashes Test at Headingley in 2023. With Australia 2-0 up in the series, Wood averaged 90.4mph on day one and transformed the series in an electric spell of pace bowling, famously dismissing Australia opener Usman Khawaja.

"I was absolutely ready to go. The day before I was bowling to a mitt and the strength coach had to swap because it was hurting his hand so much.

"I can still hear the commentary and feel the ball.

"It was a special moment because my parents were here as well. It was the first time they saw me get five wickets.

"I spent a lot of my career in the bouncer role. I thought at times I was better than that and it hurt my stats.

"That day I got to pitch it up and it was the swing that did it.

"The BBC had [the Khawaja wicket] on socials and I watched it so many times. I just loved the noise it made. I wish I could bottle that up."

articles.body:
South Africa posted 297-8 in their 50 overs and Australia were well ​on course after a fast start, until poor shot selection caused their charge to collapse and they finished on 230 all out, losing ​their last nine wickets for 101 runs.

Australia will welcome the ‌likely return of captain Pat Cummins for the second match in the three-game series in Johannesburg on Sunday, live on Sky Sports , but ​if this series is a fact-finding mission ahead of the 2027 Cricket World Cup in South Africa, Namibia and Zimbabwe, there will be much food for thought.

"I'm pretty ​disappointed," Australia captain Mitch Marsh said. "South Africa outplayed us. It was ⁠a good game of cricket but we ⁠fell well short.

"We had our opportunities, I am probably going to sound like a broken record speaking about having partnerships in our ‌batting, but we weren't able to form many tonight."

Australia won the toss and decided to bowl, strangling the South African run-rate early on.

But when Breetzke came in at number ‌four, he played conventional cricket shots to get his innings started, before he found a willing partner in big-hitting Marco Jansen.

Breetzke, who averages over 60 with the bat in his 15 ODIs, scored his 112 from 106 deliveries and Jansen equalled his career best with ⁠75 in 59 deliveries.

Australia started their innings in brilliant fashion as Marsh ​blasted 60 from 36 balls and put on 90 in ​9.2 overs for the first wicket with Travis Head (36 from 37 balls).

But ​too many batters threw their wickets away at the top of the order.

Jansen's sensational ⁠diving one-handed catch in the outfield to dismiss Matt Renshaw (44) left Australia on 215-7, a position they never recovered from.

South African spinners Keshav Maharaj (4-20 in 9.2 overs) and Bjorn Fortuin (2-34 in ⁠8) showed excellent control.

"Very satisfied, all round it ​was a good fight from the batters and bowlers," South Africa captain Temba ​Bavuma said.

"Looking at how both innings started, we were under pressure in the first 10 overs in each, but we managed to get ‌a very competitive score on ​that wicket."

articles.title: England vs Sri Lanka: Jos Buttler's bravery in vain as tourists fight back to level series
articles.summary: Jos Buttler's bravery comes in vain as Sri Lanka fight back to beat England in the second one-day international at Headingley and set up a series decider at The Oval.
articles.body:
Second Metro Bank one-day international, Headingley

Sri Lanka 321-6 (50 overs): Kusal 121, Kamindu 54; Ahmed 2-48

England 305-9 (50 overs): Banton 73, Buttler 69; Wellalage 3-49

Jos Buttler's bravery came in vain as Sri Lanka fought back to beat England in the second one-day international at Headingley and set up a series decider at The Oval.

Needing 68 from 75 balls, England were cruising towards a target of 322 until Buttler retired hurt on 67 after tweaking a hamstring.

When Rehan Ahmed, Gus Atkinson and Jamie Overton fell, Buttler re-emerged with 27 needed from 14 balls and witnessed Will Jacks fall for 52 at the non-striker's end.

England were left needing 19 from the last with Buttler on strike but, barely able to hobble a single, he holed out at deep mid-wicket. England finished on 306-9 as Sri Lanka won by 16 runs.

Buttler had earlier shown flashes of his vintage best in hitting Sri Lanka's spinners for five sixes, putting England on course after collapse of 3-14 spoiled an opening stand of 143 between Tom Banton and Ben Duckett.

Sri Lanka were fortunate for the way he was abruptly halted but deserve credit for the way their seamers used reverse swing afterwards to deny England's lower order.

Their captain Kusal Mendis also hit a fine 122 in their 321-6. The series, and the international summer, concludes on Sunday from 10:30 BST.

'The lads wanted me to stick one up him' - Wood relives fastest spells

Sri Lanka level ODI series as England fall short in thriller - as it happened

Pick your County Championship team of the season

What to make of this dramatic encounter? It is a defeat for England, one which halts their momentum a touch as they build towards next year's 50-over World Cup.

It was unlike any other, however. They will do well to find situations like these again when the bigger moments come.

"It is always disappointing when you lose," captain Harry Brook said.

"Sri Lanka played exceptionally well there, especially the last 10-15 overs. There were plenty of moments in the game we could have been slightly better."

One positive was the batting of Buttler before injury struck. He has not scored a century in this format for three-and-a-half years and had his T20 form doubted earlier this year at the World Cup.

The way he took down the spinners was brutal. When he was flying, England were on course for their highest chase at this ground.

The opening stand between Banton and Duckett was also impressive - reminiscent of England's brightest ODIs days as they thrashed around the bowling at more than seven runs an over.

That neither pressed on - Duckett was bowled for 67 and Banton stumped for 73, both to left-arm spinner Dinuth Wellalage - was disappointing. There were also rare failures for Joe Root who made 15 and Brook, the latter also pinned in front lbw for one by Wellalage.

Perhaps more concerning was that the lower order were unable to support Jacks in his quest to push England over the line again.

That aspect must improve over England's three white-ball series that come before mid-January.

This has been a difficult tour for Sri Lanka, who were outclassed in the 3-0 T20 series defeat and well beaten by 89 runs in the first ODI at Chester-le-Street.

This, especially given the bad start with the ball, will be a significant boost to morale.

Kusal was troubled early on by Overton's bouncers, top-edging one into a gap soon after Atkinson dropped a simple chance at fine leg when the right-hander had 17 - another England error. The Sri Lanka captain also had to overturn a caught-behind decision on 99 when Overton was the bowler again.

Kusal was eventually caught on the boundary trying to clear deep mid-wicket off Ahmed, who also had Charith Asalanka caught in the same position for 2-48 but did not offer the control usually brought by Adil Rashid.

A flat Headingley pitch was a far bigger test of England's seamers than Tuesday's difficult surface in Durham.

Josh Tongue struggled with his lines for 0-50 in seven overs. Atkinson, who took 2-55, and Overton, who had another catch dropped in the final over, in taking 0-63 from 10 were England's best bowling performers.

"Tight games are always good games to watch and good games to be a part of," Brook added.

"Having the opportunity to play in a decider will only benefit us."

articles.title: IPL bets, affairs, loans, lavish lifestyle: Killer 'son' emerges from shadows as Kanpur bizman murder case takes major twist
articles.summary: KANPUR: IPL betting, mounting loans, a lavish lifestyle and a fear that his father’s property could go to another woman — investigators say these strands
articles.body: KANPUR: IPL betting, mounting loans, a lavish lifestyle and a fear that his father’s property could go to another woman — investigators say these strands came together in the alleged plot to kill 63-year-old pharmaceutical trader Vineet Minocha.Police have now arrested his 34-year-old son Subrat, alleging that he masterminded the conspiracy and hired two men to carry out the murder.Police alleged that Subrat had accumulated debts of more than Rs 40 lakh through gambling and IPL betting and was also involved in intoxicants.According to investigators, Subrat received around Rs 40,000 every month from his father for his expenses but was paying about Rs 55,000 a month towards loan instalments. Police said his father had become an obstacle to the lifestyle Subrat wanted to maintain.Another strand of the alleged motive was Vineet’s personal life. Police said Subrat feared that his father, who had strained relations with his current wife, might marry another woman and transfer his property to her. Vineet’s wife was staying with their daughter outside Uttar Pradesh, investigators said.Police alleged that Subrat therefore decided to get his father killed. According to investigators, the original plan was to make Vineet’s death appear accidental or natural, but it was later changed. Vishal Gautam, a former employee of Vineet, allegedly agreed to carry out the killing with the help of his associate Rajkishore.Vineet was stabbed 26 times at his Ratan Orbit apartment in Kanpur’s Kalyanpur area on September 5. Police said Vishal and Rajkishore entered the flat posing as medicine delivery men before attacking him and later escaped by scaling a wall.The two men were arrested shortly after the murder and subsequently named Vineet’s daughter-in-law Shalu Minocha as the alleged conspirator. Shalu was arrested along with them. Police had initially suspected that she had hired the killers for Rs 6 lakh.The investigation, however, took a different turn after police questioned the three accused during their 24-hour custody. Investigators said call records showed more than 300 conversations between Subrat and Vishal, the highest number among the contacts examined in the case.Police also found that Vishal had obtained a new SIM card on September 3, two days before the murder, and allegedly made his first call from the new number to Subrat. Investigators also recovered deleted chats between the two and said their locations had coincided at several points before the killing.Police alleged that Subrat and Vishal had attempted to divert suspicion towards Shalu. Vishal reportedly told investigators that Subrat had asked him to kill his father and promised him Rs 6 lakh. He also allegedly claimed that Subrat had instructed him to name Shalu if the conspiracy was uncovered.Police are verifying these allegations through call records, digital evidence and other material. Commissioner of police Raghubir Lal said Subrat had not confessed to the murder and that all scientific, digital, CCTV, call-detail and circumstantial evidence would be independently scrutinised.The latest developments have also put Shalu’s alleged role under fresh scrutiny. Police said they had so far not found sufficient corroborative evidence establishing her involvement, though she has not been given a clean chit.“Whether she is complicit or not will be decided by the court,” a senior police officer said.Investigators have also recovered a duplicate key to Vineet’s flat from Vishal. articles.summary: The on-field confrontation between India opener Yashasvi Jaiswal and Sri Lanka pacer Asitha Fernando during the second Test in Colombo had become one of
articles.body: The on-field confrontation between India opener Yashasvi Jaiswal and Sri Lanka pacer Asitha Fernando during the second Test in Colombo had become one of the talking points of the series. Nearly a month after the incident, India wicketkeeper-batter Dhruv Jurel has revealed what Jaiswal told him about the exchange.The incident took place during the opening session on Day 1 of the second Test. Jaiswal was batting aggressively on 45 and had already struck Fernando for three boundaries in the over before the Sri Lankan pacer dismissed him with the final delivery of the 17th over.Fernando celebrated the wicket with an animated send-off as Jaiswal began walking back towards the dressing room. However, the Indian batter soon turned around and walked back towards the Sri Lankan pacer, leading to a heated confrontation.'He didn't say anything'The two players came face-to-face before teammates and the Sri Lankan captain intervened to separate them. Jurel has now claimed that Jaiswal told him Fernando had been verbally abusing him continuously following the dismissal.“When he got out, he was quietly walking back to the dressing room. He didn't say anything. If you look at the footage, Jaiswal immediately turned around. The Sri Lankan pacer was abusing him. Jaiswal told me that he was abusing him nonstop,” Jurel told former India batter Aakash Chopra.According to Jurel, Jaiswal did not object to Fernando celebrating the wicket but drew the line at personal abuse.“Jaiswal told him, ‘It's okay. You took my wicket, you can show normal aggression, but you can't abuse me,’” Jurel added.‘He never starts it’Jurel, who is also Jaiswal's teammate at Rajasthan Royals, described the opener as someone who does not generally initiate verbal exchanges but is willing to respond when provoked.When Chopra suggested that Jaiswal is a “feisty guy” who gives it back when someone provokes him, Jurel agreed.“100 per cent. He will never start it; I have never seen him do that. He is always in the zone; he is always thinking about his batting. But if you provoke us, we will also return it,” Jurel said.The confrontation eventually required the intervention of players from both sides, bringing an end to the tense exchange on the field. articles.body: Nepal sent a warning to the rest of the competition with a stunning five-wicket upset over Afghanistan, chasing down 103 with 14 balls to spare in their Asian Games Group A opener at Korogi Sports Park on Friday. After their spinners strangled Afghanistan for just 102, Nepal recovered from a precarious 31/3 to complete a composed chase. Rohit Paudel, Sundeep Jora and captain Dipendra Singh Airee held their nerve to seal a memorable win.Nepal's chase got off to a disastrous start as they lost both openers cheaply. Afghanistan left-arm seamer Faridoon Dawoodzai dismissed Kushal Bhurtel for a duck before right-arm pacer Abdullah Ahmadzai removed Aasif Sheikh for two.Things got worse when Kushal Malla was run out in the seventh over, leaving Nepal struggling at 31/3 after 6.3 overs.Rohit, Sundeep rescue Nepal before captain finishes jobSundeep and Rohit then steadied the innings with a crucial partnership. The pair kept rotating the strike and punished loose deliveries to keep Nepal's chase alive. Sundeep smashed a four and a six across the ninth and 10th overs before being run out in the 10th, giving Afghanistan renewed hope.Rohit, however, remained composed and found a reliable partner in Dipendra. The duo avoided unnecessary risks, picking up singles and twos as Nepal moved steadily towards the target.With victory within touching distance, Rohit accelerated and hit three fours across the 16th and 17th overs. Dipendra fell in the 18th over with Nepal level with Afghanistan's total, but Gulsan Jha calmly collected a single to complete the chase.Rohit finished unbeaten on 33 off 32 balls, while Sundeep made 34 off 35 and Dipendra contributed 15 off 18.Afghanistan's batting collapses under spin pressureEarlier, Nepal's spinners had put Afghanistan under pressure from the outset. Kushal Bhurtel and Lalit Rajbanshi shared seven wickets between them, preventing Afghanistan's batters from building significant partnerships.Rajbanshi was particularly economical, finishing with three wickets for just 13 runs from his four overs, while Bhurtel claimed four wickets as Afghanistan struggled to score freely.
