articles.title: Kevin Pietersen: Former England batter on Harry Brook and working with Test side before Ashes
articles.summary: Former batter turned specialist mentor Kevin Pietersen talks about his new role with England, his past history with the ECB and working with Harry Brook and Brendon McCullum.
articles.body:
Kevin Pietersen is asked, after everything that came before, what he would have said if told he would work for the England and Wales Cricket board again one day.

In 2014, he was sacked by the ECB in one of most ugly and acrimonious periods in English cricketing history – a period that brought one of the most exciting but divisive international careers to an end.

"What do you think I'd have said," Pietersen says with a smile.

Bigger stars in English cricket are harder to find.

This is the man who had a brief but high-profile relationship with American celebrity Caprice, married a pop star, Jessica from Liberty X, and once tried to explain cricket to Taylor Swift on The Graham Norton Show.

Back in the dressing room as a mentor, he is speaking to the media at Headingley - the location of his famous "it's tough being me" press conference.

The hair is greyer, but he still carries all of that aura.

"I'm 46, man," he says, asked whether animosity remains.

"That stuff is so long gone. I am a completely different person.

"I live in South Africa. I love doing what I do. I am just here to help Brendon first and foremost, help the players try and become the best versions of themselves."

Listen to Pietersen's interview with Test Match Special

My preconceptions of England 'completely different' to reality

Pietersen was the most intriguing of appointments to England's dressing room staff because of his own history, but also what he has said before.

While commentating on England's white-ball tour of India last year, he suggested the Brendon McCullum outfit were not training enough.

"Clearly the perceptions I had before being asked to do the job were completely different to what I feel now," he says.

"It is nice to being part of an England team and set-up that is actually really, really driven."

Pietersen answers every question with poise. Almost all are given and lengthy, considered responses.

His only terse response comes when pushed on what exactly those preconceptions were - and how quickly they took to disappear.

"You know what the preconceptions were," he says. "I am not going near it."

I can help these players 'stay away from the ugly'

Despite that, he appears to be loving his return.

Pietersen is "not sitting here wanting to be the coach of England" but wants to help McCullum and the players, many of whom grew up idolising him.

One of those, Tom Banton, said last week he is still in awe of the four-time Ashes-winner, so much so he was struggling to build up the courage to speak to him.

"He wants a YouTube channel," Pietersen laughs. Pietersen, a 50-over great who played in a way ahead of his time, can also help him there.

His official title is "specialist mentor" and he will dip in and out to work with the white-ball teams through to the 50-over World Cup next autumn.

Before the first ODI in Durham, England posted a clip on social media of Pietersen leading a batting session.

Holding court, he had Joe Root and Rehan Ahmed alike involved in a batting drill on how to rotate the strike against spin.

"All I want to be is a great person to these guys," Pietersen says.

"I want to be the best guy in the room, so that they come to me, and they ask me for information, and if I've got stuff for them, I'll give it to them.

"I am lucky to have worn every T-shirt an England cricketer can wear – the good, the bad the ugly.

"I can potentially help them to stay away from the ugly."

Pietersen's eyes roll slightly when he is asked about Ben Stokes' recent comments comparing Harry Brook's talents to his.

Pietersen, like Brook, was a maverick – a batter capable of incredible highs. Those highs mean the lows come with a disproportionate level of criticism.

"Where I can help him is playing situations, because there was a lot of method in my madness," Pietersen says.

"Yes, occasionally, I got out to reckless shots and crazy shots in the '80s and '90s but there was a lot of structure to the way that I batted.

"I've still got notes on my phone on how I played in T20 cricket, one-day cricket, Test match cricket, and about hitting straight back at the stumps, and the techniques, and how I did it, and don't play certain shots.

"That all-round structure is something I could potentially help him with because he's so flipping good.

"It's actually frightening how good he is and how good he can be."

And Pietersen says he will not limit himself to working purely on white-ball cricket.

He has already spoken to new Test coach Stephen Fleming about how he can help the Test batters during his time with the white-ball squads.

Though he said he would not have time for a full-time role, he suggested he is open to working with the Test side before next summer's home Ashes series.

"I have got a pretty mad schedule," he says. "I wouldn't say no.

"I don't think that necessarily means I need to be in a dressing room.

"There is a lot of time in the lead up to an Ashes series and a tour of South Africa, when I will be with the Test batters.

"There are conversations I can have there."

Who knows how long this will last. England may as well make the most of this second chance.

articles.title: Kevin Pietersen says he is "completely different person" after taking England role and hints at role ahead of Ashes
articles.summary: Kevin Pietersen says he "wouldn't say no" to the opportunity to contribute to England's coaching team for next year's Ashes against Australia; Pietersen recently made a surprise return to the England set-up as a specialist on the white-ball coaching staff
articles.body:
Pietersen represented England 277 times across all formats during his playing days, but was sacked in 2014 and has since been disconnected from the side for more than a decade after the ECB accused him of failing to support captain Sir Alastair Cook following the 5-0 Ashes defeat in Australia.

He was also dropped in 2012 after sending texts to the South African team, and since retiring has been a vocal critic of England, accusing the white-ball team of poor preparation ahead of last January's tour of India.

Having recently returned to the England set up as a specialist on the white-ball coaching staff, Pietersen is keen to offer his talents and experience to the current crop of England stars.

"I'm 46, man. That stuff's so long gone. I'm a completely different person too," he said.

"I've been lucky to have worn every t-shirt an England cricketer can wear; the good, the bad, and the ugly. There are parts to all of their careers, which I think that I could potentially help them to stay away from the ugly.

"I'm in the two ears, one mouth phase. I listen twice as much as I talk. I've seen a lot, I've done a lot, and I want to be the best guy in the room for these guys

"(White ball head coach McCullum) loves being challenged on different opinions. Whether he uses it or not, that's up to him. He is the head coach. I'm not sitting here wanting to be the coach of England. He's the coach of England. If I can help him, in his journey, in his pursuit, in our pursuit, to be competitive next year then it's a win."

Pietersen joined the coaching staff ahead of the ongoing series against Sri Lanka and will serve as a specialist mentor through to the 2027 Cricket World Cup in Africa.

Recalling his first conversation with McCullum, he said: "I thought I was in trouble," he said of his first conversation with Brendon McCullum. "'What have I done now? Why is he calling me?'

"We talked about how critical I had been of the setup. It took a couple of weeks of conversations with him to be able to convince me that it was something that I wanted to do because the perception wasn't actually the reality that I now know, about what is in that dressing room. These guys are really, really driven.

"It's amazing to be back in an England dressing room and it's amazing to be back with these guys. They are very, very eager to learn. They want to be the best versions of themselves."

Pietersen also suggested there is a chance he could contribute to England's red ball activity when new Test coach Stephen Fleming leads his team into next year's Ashes.

"I've got a pretty mad schedule, (but) I wouldn't say no," he explained.

"I have had a conversation with Stephen, but I don't think that necessarily means that I need to be in a dressing room. There's a lot of time in the lead up to an Ashes series. There's a lot of time in the lead up to the tour of South Africa, where I'm going to be with the Test players, the Test batters in Australia, and there's conversations that can be had there.

"I've certainly had conversations with Flem, who I absolutely love, about language that he would like me to use with the Test batters, going into South Africa, and then certainly into the summer next year. I just don't think I can commit to a lot more time."

articles.body:
An ECB spokesperson said: "Surrey batter Dan Lawrence has been called into the England Men's squad for Sunday's third Metro Bank ODI against Sri Lanka.

Lawrence has been withdrawn from Surrey's County Championship fixture against Somerset and is set to train with England at The Oval on Saturday morning.

Sri Lanka showed great fight to halt the hosts' chase in the second ODI and secure a 16-run victory at Headingley, levelling the three-match series at 1-1. Buttler played a decisive role in the hosts' chase before his injury ruled him out of the series decider.

Buttler had looked set to guide the hosts towards victory before pulling up in the 38th over with England 254-4. He was forced to retire hurt but returned to the crease in the 48th over in a final attempt to rescue the chase. Despite the injury, he went on to make 69 before being dismissed.

Will Jacks (52), Rehan Ahmed (0), Gus Atkinson (16) and Jamie Overton (2) also fell as the hosts' hopes faded. England managed just one four and one six from the 37th over onwards as Sri Lanka's bowlers tightened the pressure to seal a hard-fought win.

With the series finely poised at 1-1, the hosts must now regroup for the decider without Buttler, who played a central role in their second ODI chase.

articles.title: County Championship: Hain ton edges Bears nearer to 2026 title
articles.summary: Centurion Sam Hain shares a 165-run stand with skipper Ed Barnard against Leicestershire to edge Warwickshire close to a ninth County Championship title.
articles.body:
Rothesay County Championship, Division One, Edgbaston (day two)

Leicestershire 125 & 55-3: Budinger 43*; Bamber 2-27

Warwickshire 372: Hain 142, Barnard 88; A Patel 3-78

Leicestershire (3 pts) trail Warwickshire (6 pts) by 192 runs

Sam Hain hit a splendid day two century against relegation-threatened Leicestershire at Edgbaston to keep Warwickshire on course to win a ninth County Championship title.

In seamer-friendly conditions, Hain compiled a highly-skilled 142 from 301 balls - his 21st century in first-class cricket - as the Bears reached 372 to take a substantial first-innings lead of 247.

Hain, who reached his 1,000 first-class runs for the season, for only the second time, was well supported by Ed Barnard who made 88 in a partnership of 165 in 50 overs.

Leicestershire, rolled for 125 first time round, then closed on 55-3 after Bears paceman Ethan Bamber took two more wickets to take his season's tally to 66.

A draw would now be enough to secure the title but the home supporters, who have turned out in force on the first two days, will arrive for the third expecting a fourth to be unnecessary.

Foxes relegated by Bears, subject to points appeal

Championship titles are constructed on a bedrock of solid sessions interspersed with the occasional spectacular one - and Hain and Barnard's efforts were the epitome of solid.

Resuming on 130-4, already five runs in front, they added 51 without loss in a morning session truncated by bad light.

Hain and Barnard did exactly what their team required, advancing steadily to lay the platform for a big lead and potential innings victory.

The Bears' fifth-wicket pair continued to concentrate hard after lunch until, with the lead already 126, Barnard departed livid with himself at edging a big drive at a wide ball from Ben Green - just 12 shy of a century.

Chris Woakes chipped his second ball to mid-on, but Kai Smith and Manny Suthar enjoyed useful cameos before also falling to the persevering Hull.

They had accompanied the excellent Hain towards his century which was greeted by a standing ovation from the big audience, then Bamber added further useful runs before being bowled by a beauty from Patel.

Even then the Foxes' frustration went on as last pair Hain and Olly Hannon-Dalby added 35.

Leicestershire opener Sol Budinger then came out firing, hitting 43 not out off 36 balls, But Bamber struck twice in three balls, trapping Sheridon Gumbs and then flattening Rishi Patel's off-stump two balls late.

After a bad-light interruption, Woakes then pinned Steve Eskinazi lbw in the gloom to leave Warwickshire maybe only one strong session away from the title.

ECB Reporters' Network supported by Rothesay.

articles.title: County Championship: Sam Hain leads Warwickshire's bid for title-clinching win over Leicestershire at Edgbaston
articles.summary: Friday's County Championship sees Warwickshire move ever closer to title after moving into lead of 192 runs against relegation-threatened Leicestershire at Edgbaston at the end of day two; Warwickshire win would guarantee a first title since the Covid-shortened 2021 campaign
articles.body:
Warwickshire needed at least 14 points from their final match of the season and have already taken six bonus points after skittling Leicestershire for 125 on day one before Hain led the home side to 372 all out in reply.

Leicestershire, who slipped to 55-3 in their second innings at close, are all but relegated, subject to their appeal against a 27-point deduction for a substandard pitch at Grace Road last month.

Second-placed Somerset's title hopes appear over - they began their last fixture 11 points behind Warwickshire - even if they beat Surrey at Taunton.

Surrey extended their overnight 327-4 to 422 all out, with Dan Lawrence finally out for 139, before Somerset's Tom Lammonby made 103 not out as the hosts reached 222-3 - a 200-run deficit at the game's midway stage.

Nottinghamshire's title defence also appears over despite bowling out Yorkshire for 179 in reply to the hosts' 251 all out and after reaching 55-3 at close, the home side lead by 127 runs.

Glamorgan reached 505 all out in Cardiff - Asa Tribe made 184 - before reducing Essex to 100-7 and relegated Hampshire trail Sussex by 332 runs at the Utilita Bowl after the visitors reached 216-5 in their second innings, with Tom Haines set to resume on 99.

In Division Two, Kent are on course to seal promotion behind title winners Durham as they lead by 63 runs against bottom club Gloucestershire .

Kent opener Ben Compton made 126 to help Kent reach 353 all out and the visitors are 61-2 in their second innings.

Promotion hopefuls Northamptonshire face an uphill task at Lord's having been restricted to 249-7 for a 97-run lead over Middlesex with three wickets in hand.

Bad light at Old Trafford meant Lancashire made only 10 without loss in reply to Durham's first-innings total of 493 all out.

Resuming on 355-5, the champions were further boosted by half-centuries from Ollie Robinson and Brydon Carse, the latter ending on 58 not out.

Worcestershire's Matthew Waite will resume on 73 after helping his side reach 203-9 in their second innings for a lead of 329, having skittled Derbyshire for 88 on the first day.

articles.title: Alonso hits two more HRs in 10-2 Orioles win over Yanks
articles.summary: Pete Alonso’s ridiculous tear at the plate continued in a Yankee Stadium rout.
articles.body:
This just in, ladies and gentlemen: Pete Alonso is really good at baseball.

The Most Valuable Oriole continued to be the best thing to happen to this franchise in a long time, adding two more homers to his league-leading total in a 10-2 blowout win to open a doubleheader against the Yankees.

Whatever other things have gone wrong for the Orioles this year — and oh boy, are there many — Pete Alonso has been worth the price of admission all by himself. Tonight, even in a game that had no meaning for either team, he proved why.

Alonso stepped to the plate with a man aboard in the third against Yankees starter Brendan Beck, who'd begun the game with two scoreless innings. Pete put an end to that real quick. He drove a 407-foot dinger into the left-field seats, his 42nd of the year. At that point, Alonso's last seven hits had all been dingers. Did I mention this guy is good at baseball?

The Orioles turned the game into a laugher in the fourth even without Pete being prominently involved (though he did get a single). The O's loaded the bases with nobody out for the soft underbelly of the lineup, including Christian Franklin and Carlos Narváez , who entered the game with a combined zero RBIs in 132 plate appearances with the Orioles. That's Caleb Joseph territory right there. Franklin managed to get off the schneid with a sharp single to right, collecting his first major league RBI, but Narváez remained in his drought by hitting into a force at the plate.

It shouldn't be that hard to get one measly RBI, Carlos. Just watch as Dylan Beavers gets four of them in one at-bat! The O's right fielder jumped on a hanging curveball from Beck and clobbered it into the right-field seats for his first career grand slam. Beavers! With one mighty swing, the Orioles had an insurmountable 7-0 lead.

The Birds' victory was all but assured, but that doesn't mean they couldn't have some more fun along the way. In the top of the sixth, Jeremiah Jackson lofted a fly ball to deep center field. Spencer Jones loped back at an ambling pace, as if he had the ball tracked all the way, but when he reached up to make the catch, it glanced off his glove and deflected to the wall. The ball trickled along the warning track for so long that Jackson just kept circling the bases, and by the time the Yankees got the ball into the infield, Jackson had slid in safely with an inside-the-park home run.

Look at the wheels on Jeremiah! If you'd told me that the Orioles would have two inside-the-parkers this season and they'd be hit by Coby Mayo and Jeremiah Jackson, I'm not sure I would've believed you. This has been a strange season, occasionally in good ways.

You know what's not strange? Pete Alonso being awesome. It's just what he does, and always has. Alonso led off the seventh against reliever Yerry de los Santos and absolutely demolished a baseball. Holy smokes, was it tattooed, a mammoth blast the landed high into the left-field bleacher seats.

Pete, that baseball had a family! The blast was his second of the game and AL-leading 43rd of the year, and extended his AL-leading RBI count to 112. In all likelihood, Pete is going to take two of the three Triple Crown categories. He won't win AL MVP, and I'm not saying he should, but…is there any player in the American League who's really that much better than him? I'd put him in my top five for sure.

This game was all Orioles, but if there was one disappointing aspect, it's that Trevor Rogers didn't get the chance to earn the win in what may well have been his final start as an Oriole. Rogers pitched brilliantly tonight as always, but the Orioles, in an apparently pre-planned move, removed him from the game after four innings and 55 pitches.

I mean…why? Rogers was showing no signs of fatigue. He mowed down the Yankees in the first four frames, throwing 41 strikes and just 14 balls. He allowed only one run, on an Amed Rosario RBI single in the fourth, and the O's had a comfortable six-run lead when he left. Was his arm really going to fall off if he threw more than 55 pitches in his final start of the season?

I will grant that he'd already thrown a career-high 169.2 innings this season, and perhaps the Orioles saw no reason to push him in a meaningless game, but I would've let him at least pitch one more inning to get a W next to his name. Mostly I just don't want to accept that this might've been the last time we see Rogers in an Orioles uniform.

The Orioles hit double digits in runs on Gunnar Henderson 's RBI single in the eighth that deflected off the second baseman, and the bullpen took it from there. Albert Suárez , now in his sixth stint with the Orioles this year, did his usual quality work in long relief. He tossed four scoreless innings and struck out five, even despite a nosebleed that afflicted him in the eighth. Suárez has been an unsung hero of the O's bullpen, constantly eating up innings without complaint even when he knows he'll probably get DFA'd the next day, then inevitably returning to the roster to do it all over again.

Alex Hoppe 's ninth inning was a mess — 22 pitches, two walks, and a run — but a nine-run lead gives you plenty of wiggle room, and he eventually finished it with a called strikeout of Ben Rice . Orioles win, 10-2. Not a bad way to start the weekend.

articles.title: ‘It starts now:’ Morne Morkel sets India’s World Cup tone ahead of WI series
articles.summary: THIRUVANANTHAPURAM: India’s bowling coach Morne Morkel used the pre-series press conference in Thiruvananthapuram on Friday to frame the three-match ODI
articles.body: THIRUVANANTHAPURAM: India’s bowling coach Morne Morkel used the pre-series press conference in Thiruvananthapuram on Friday to frame the three-match ODI series against West Indies as the opening move of a much bigger campaign, one that ends with the 2027 World Cup in South Africa. His message was simple: The standards India wants to carry into next year’s showpiece tournament cannot be switched on later.“You can’t decide a month or a week before a World Cup that you’re going to step things up. It starts now, with this series against the West Indies. I want to see guys putting their hands up for the ball, wanting to create pressure and not protecting their own space,” Morkel said.No player drew more questions than allrounder Nitish Kumar Reddy, whose path to a full bowling workload, after a series of recurring injuries, remains one of India’s more delicate management projects. Morkel admitted that the challenge was turning instinct into something repeatable.“He is a talented guy when it comes to bat, ball and field. He always wants to be the guy who creates opportunities, and having that mindset is fantastic. But the role we want him to play is about consistency and how well he can do the basics,” the former South African pacer explained.With a relatively open stretch of a calendar ahead, Morkel reckoned the plan is to keep giving Reddy a well-defined job, as he builds towards competing properly for India’s allrounder’s spot.With Hardik Pandya and Harshit Rana working their way back from injuries, workload management remains a core issue for the coaching staff. Morkel said the medical team and coaches are mapping out individual plans for every bowler in a wider pool, with an eye on the next year’s World Cup.“There is definitely a plan for every individual, and we will keep monitoring that, coming up with the best way forward to give the selectors the best group to pick from,” Morkel elaborated.With Shubman Gill continuing as captain and Virat Kohli back after a break, Morkel was asked how India balances settled young leadership with a wealth of experience. He credited Gill’s captaincy while stressing the value of senior players as informal mentors around the squad.“Shubman’s done an exceptional job leading the team. Different players feel more comfortable speaking to different senior guys, and we’re fortunate to have that experience in the group. articles.title: Anshul Kamboj exploits tricky Puducherry pitch as India ‘A’ beat Australia ‘A’
articles.summary: PUDUCHERRY: The heat in Puducherry was unforgiving. The pitch offered little movement for the pace bowlers.
articles.body: PUDUCHERRY: The heat in Puducherry was unforgiving. The pitch offered little movement for the pace bowlers. Yet, India ‘A’ paceman Anshul Kamboj found a way to make things work.Kamboj was the first to strike in the morning session, using the cracks and variable bounce to dismiss Australia ‘A’ batters Nathan McSweeney and Peter Handscomb in consecutive overs to set up a 162-run win in the first unofficial Test here on Friday. McSweeney was surprised by the extra bounce before Handscomb was beaten by one that stayed low and crashed into the off stump.Left-arm spinner Shams Mulani (3-57) and medium-pacer Tushar Deshpande (3-14) took three wickets apiece as the Aussies folded for 200 while chasing 363 in the last innings.Kamboj, after returning figures of 2-25, said that the conditions were difficult for the pacers. “It was too hot for fast bowling. You have to put in a lot of effort to maintain the intensity. I am very happy that I am able to maintain that,” Kamboj said after the win.The surface, with its “whitish soil” and limited bounce, demanded discipline and an understanding of the areas to bowl in. “This is whitish soil. So here it was just that we always have to keep the wickets in play and bowl within stumps,” he said.Kamboj first underlined his red-ball credentials with an eight-wicket innings haul in Duleep Trophy and then produced a 10-wicket innings haul against Kerala in Ranji Trophy in 2024. His reward came in July 2025 when he was handed his Test debut at Old Trafford. He took 1-89 before being left out after that.Kamboj, though, refuses to see one match as a setback. “I am not trying to change anything. If one or two matches go wrong in your career, it doesn’t mean that you are bad. Everyone can see your hard work. If I just keep working hard, the results will fall in favour,” the 25-year-old said.He was also CSK’s leading wicket-taker in the 2026 season, finishing with 21 scalps. Now he has another opportunity to take his game to another level under new head coach Zaheer Khan. “I am very excited to meet him. I had a camp with him in CoE in Bengaluru.”Brief scores: India ‘A’ 334 & 199. Australia ‘A’ 171 & 200 (F O'Neill 47; T Deshpande 3-14, S Mulani 3-57). articles.title: DDCA joint secretary raises concerns over Delhi selector, support staff appointments
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Delhi & District Cricket Association (DDCA) joint secretary Amit Grover has formally raised reservations over the proposed appointments of
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Delhi & District Cricket Association (DDCA) joint secretary Amit Grover has formally raised reservations over the proposed appointments of Varun Sood and Manu Nayyar as part of the Delhi cricket setup, questioning whether they meet the prescribed eligibility criteria.In an email sent to members of the Cricket Advisory Committee (CAC) on Friday, a copy of which TimesofIndia.com has, Grover said he wanted to place his concerns on record before the selection process concluded. He urged the committee to examine the relevant records and applicable rules before making any final decision on the proposed appointments. The email is addressed to members of the CAC and copied to the DDCA top brass.“With regard to the proposed appointments of coaches and selectors, I wish to formally place on record my reservations concerning the proposed appointment of Mr. Varun Sood and Mr. Manu Nayyar, particularly with regard to their eligibility and compliance with the prescribed criteria,” Grover wrote in the email.Manu Nayyar has been appointed as selector for the senior men’s team and Varun Sood as assistant coach for the men’s U-19 team. It is worth noting that there was an issue with Nayyar's availability last season as he was reportedly missing due to committments in an overseas league, when the teams were being picked at DDCA.“All the rules have been followed diligently. Everyone who has been appointed has played cricket at the highest level. They have been in the system for a long time. Manu Nayyar is yet to complete his five-year term, whereas Varun has recently retired from playing cricket and knows a thing or two about how modern-day cricket functions. We are all thinking about the betterment of Delhi cricket, and these accusations are needless,” said a recipient of the email.TimesofIndia.com reached out to DDCA secretary Ashok Sharma for a comment but received no response.Former India wicketkeeper Vijay Dahiya has been reappointed as head coach of the Delhi Ranji Trophy team as the DDCA named coaches, mentors and High Performance Centre staff, with several former players and their sons also finding assignments in the appointments. There are 22 coaches, including head coaches, assistant coaches, bowling coaches and fielding coaches, appointed across the senior men’s team to the U-14 level, while 18 have been appointed across various women’s teams.Meanwhile, Grover emphasised that the concerns had been communicated before the completion of the selection process and, therefore, should be considered by the CAC before any appointment was finalised. He said the committee should satisfy itself that all eligibility conditions and prescribed criteria had been complied with.The DDCA joint secretary also questioned the proposed composition of the selection panel, pointing out that it appeared to substantially comprise the same selectors who were associated with the process last year.His concern comes against the backdrop of what he described as disappointing performances by Delhi cricket. Grover acknowledged that continuity could have its merits but urged the CAC to exercise “greater care and circumspection” while selecting coaches and selectors. He said recent performances, along with eligibility, experience and the overall requirements of Delhi cricket, should be taken into account when making the appointments.“I therefore request the CAC to independently examine all relevant records and applicable criteria before taking any final decision,” Grover wrote, while also requesting that his communication be treated as part of the official record of the selection and appointment process.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: India will face Afghanistan in the men's cricket quarter-finals at the Asian Games 2026 after Nepal topped Pool A following a rain-affected washout against Japan in Nisshin on Saturday.The result confirmed the knockout-stage line-up, with Nepal progressing as group winners and Afghanistan advancing as the second-placed side. India's quarter-final against Afghanistan is scheduled for September 28 in Nisshin, with a place in the semi-finals at stake.Nepal's explosive finish sets up washoutNepal were asked to bat first and posted an imposing 149/4 in 15 overs, with Sundeep Jora and Lokesh Bam providing a late assault. Nepal were struggling at 84/4 after 10 overs before Jora and Bam changed the complexion of the innings. Jora, who came in at No. 3, remained unbeaten on 57 off 32 balls, smashing five fours and three sixes.Bam was even more aggressive at the death, hammering an unbeaten 52 off just 22 balls, including six sixes and a four. Earlier, Aasif Sheikh gave Nepal a brisk start to the middle phase, scoring 21 off 15 balls and putting on a 55-run partnership with Jora for the second wicket.Nepal had otherwise found it difficult to build momentum, with Kushal Bhurtel, Kushal Malla and Gulsan Jha all falling for single-digit scores.Rain ends Japan's chase before it beginsJapan were set a challenging target of 150 from 15 overs, but their chase never got underway. articles.title: 'Ab tak band ho jati': Virat-Rohit retirements spark viewership debate; Sehwag explains why cricket will survive
articles.summary: Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma may have walked away from two major chapters of their India careers, but Virender Sehwag believes Indian cricket is far
articles.body: Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma may have walked away from two major chapters of their India careers, but Virender Sehwag believes Indian cricket is far bigger than the stars who dominate it.For years, fans have argued that their interest in the sport is tied to individual superstars. Sehwag, however, has heard that argument before when Sunil Gavaskar, Kapil Dev and Sachin Tendulkar called time on their careers, and says cricket survived every time.In an exclusive interview with News18, Sehwag dismissed concerns that the retirements of Kohli and Rohit from T20Is and Test cricket would lead to a significant decline in cricket viewership.‘Fans said the same for Gavaskar, Kapil, Sachin’Sehwag pointed out that similar concerns were raised whenever an iconic Indian cricketer retired.“Log kehte zaroor hain, unke fans kehte hain ki hum Virat Kohli ke liye cricket dekhte hain ya Rohit Sharma ke liye dekhte hain. Par aisa toh Sunil Gavaskar ke liye bhi kaha jata tha, Kapil Dev, Sachin Tendulkar ke liye bhi kaha jata tha,” Sehwag said.The former India opener acknowledged that some fans may watch less cricket after their favourite players retire, but argued that it does not mean the sport itself will lose its appeal.“Yet, people are still watching as much cricket as they used to before,” he added.Cricket is now more accessible than everAccording to Sehwag, one of the biggest reasons cricket continues to attract viewers is its growing accessibility. He contrasted the current viewing landscape with the era when television was the primary way for fans to follow matches. With smartphones now putting live cricket and highlights in people's hands, the sport has become easier to consume.“In fact, more people are watching now because earlier it used to come on TV, but now it is available on mobile phones. It has become even easier,” Sehwag said.‘Some of their fans won’t’Sehwag did concede that the retirements of Kohli and Rohit could affect a section of their individual fan bases.“So, to say that if this player retires, we won’t watch cricket anymore, maybe some of their fans won’t,” he said.“I have also heard people say, ‘You stopped playing, so we stopped watching,’ but that’s not really the case. They probably still watch a little bit,” he added.“Agar cricketers se hi game chal rahi hoti, toh ab tak band ho jati,” he concluded.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Mayank Yadav: Rebuilding the 150kph dream, with an eye on the 2027 ODI World Cup
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A video of Mayank Yadav training with Team India’s Test and ODI captain Shubman Gill in Mohali went viral recently on social media.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A video of Mayank Yadav training with Team India’s Test and ODI captain Shubman Gill in Mohali went viral recently on social media. It comes on the heels of the tearaway quick shifting his training base to Chandigarh, where he is working with Gaurav Sharma, the city-based physio who also serves as the head physio of IPL franchise Gujarat Titans (GT).“He reached out to me after IPL 2026. Before going to Zimbabwe, he trained in Chandigarh for three weeks. He got the desired results, and he is (now) training for the upcoming West Indies series,” Sharma tells TimesofIndia.com.Mayank has had a terrible couple of years since bursting onto the scene during IPL 2024, where he impressed with his raw pace. Then a spate of injuries derailed his career. Last year, during one of the Ranji Trophy matches at the Arun Jaitley Stadium, he joked: “Lumbar stress fracture, lower back spasm, toe injury, side strain, hamstring... rehne do bhaiya, list lambi (the list is long),” he told this reporter while getting into his car outside the stadium.Mayank’s injury woes have been compounded by freak setbacks, with the fast bowler twice picking up a new injury while recovering from another. In May 2025, for instance, he injured his toe after accidentally jamming it against the side of his bed, resulting in a laceration that later became infected.He made his comeback during IPL 2026, where his pace was low, and the trolling was immediate. Former West Indies pacer Ian Bishop came to Mayank’s defence.“To see negative comments about Mayank Yadav today is horrifying. The kid nearly lost his career & livelihood at 21yrs. Just to see him play again is huge boost. The fact that he clocked 150kph again is a miracle. At 23yrs just pray for him that he stays fit. The control will come,” Bishop wrote on X.Now, a few months later, those tracking his development closely say the youngster is consistently touching the 150kph mark again.“At this moment, Mayank is doing really well. He had a back injury. He underwent surgery for the same, and the body takes time. At present, he has no injury. I am just taking care of him so that he does not pick up any injury going forward,” says Sharma, who has also worked with Arshdeep Singh, Gurnoor Brar, Naman Dhir and Prabhsimran Singh, to name a few.“The second thing is that we are working on his workload management. We are increasing the load slowly and steadily, and he is working on it very well,” says Sharma.Mayank last played in the Delhi Premier League (DPL), where he featured in seven matches for East Delhi Riders and picked up eight wickets.It has been learnt that Mayank is bowling 10 overs in three and a half hours during his training. The spells are divided into three. With the new ball, Mayank is bowling five overs, then three, and finishes it up with two overs. Out of the 60 balls he bowls daily, he consistently touches the 150kph mark, while his average speed remains in the higher 140s.With Mayank, the first thing was how we can gradually increase his workload. And once his workload hits the peak, how do we manage it at that level so that it does not come down?Devender Sharma, who has worked with Mayank during his formative years, says Mayank has been told to be ready for the 2027 ODI World Cup.“They want him to be ready for longer formats as well. He is bowling close to 12-15 overs per day for the last six months or so,” says Devender.Gaurav explains how he has planned out a programme for Mayank and how he is going through it day by day.“With Mayank, the first thing was how we can gradually increase his workload. And once his workload hits the peak, how do we manage it at that level so that it does not come down?” he explains.“So, this is a day-by-day process. We assess what we want to see, and then we are able to do what we want them to do. That allows us to progress day by day.”Above all, Sharma feels it is all about confidence, especially when it comes to Mayank, who has gone through so many injuries in his young career.“Definitely, working with a fast bowler is a challenge. With a fast bowler, there are very different biomechanics, so the chances of injury are higher. If we take into account the toll on the joints, muscles and body, and understand the mechanics of the bowler, his action and his lifestyle, then it becomes easier to work with him,” he says.“And when it comes to Mayank, we are talking about an India player. The most important thing for them is confidence. He wants to know whether I am able to give him that confidence and whether I have the answer to the question he has come to me with. I have to be very truthful with myself.“If I am giving an answer, I have to be absolutely sure that the answer is right. It cannot be hypothetical. If I am research-oriented and I know what I am doing, I should also be able to prove it in the future. That is the most important thing. Then, day by day, when we work together, that trust is built because the results of the assessment become visible. That is how things work,” he adds.For Mayank, the road back is no longer about proving how fast he can bowl. He has already shown that he can set the speed guns on fire. The bigger challenge now is sustaining that pace, building the workload required for the longer formats and, most importantly, staying on the park. With the 2027 ODI World Cup in the near future, the process has begun.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'I'm not going to worry about expectations': Virat Kohli reveals how he plans to bat in new ODI role
articles.summary: Virat Kohli is back in his favourite format, but this time without the weight of expectations and the constant chase for milestones hanging over him.
articles.body: Virat Kohli is back in his favourite format, but this time without the weight of expectations and the constant chase for milestones hanging over him. As he prepares to return to ODI cricket against the West Indies, the soon-to-be 38-year-old says he has consciously chosen to play with greater freedom and focus on what he has done best for India for years, stabilising an innings before shifting gears.Kohli has been in outstanding form in his last 10 ODIs, scoring three centuries, a 90-plus knock and four fifties. His recent performances have underlined the impact of a simpler role, with the former India captain looking increasingly comfortable as a one-format player.‘I promised myself I’m going to play more freely’Speaking to Jiostar ahead of the first ODI against the West Indies, Kohli explained what has changed in his approach.“What's changed is, firstly, I promised myself that I'm going to play more freely. I'm not going to worry about the expectations that people might have around me. My role had always been, for a long period of time, that I'm going to stabilise things,” Kohli said.The former India captain acknowledged that he has always possessed the ability to attack, but the demands of the situation often require him to take a more measured approach.“I know I can play, I know I can hit shots. But the demands are such that if it's a tricky situation and you are playing on a tricky pitch, you eventually get into a space where you're like, I can hit, but I've been given a role,” he explained.Kohli wants to add ‘30-40 extra runs’Rather than forcing himself to attack from the outset, Kohli wants to create a situation where he can maximise his contribution once he is set.“I am making a conscious effort that if I'm set to make a difference in the game, where you can get 30–40 extra runs. I want to stay in a space where, if I'm choosing not to take a risk, it's because I'm setting up eventually to get to a point where I say, okay, now press the accelerator down,” he said.Kohli backs young captain GillKohli also had words of encouragement for India's ODI captain Shubman Gill, who is still establishing himself in the leadership role.“Shubman, the captain, is still learning. He is still young in the role, but he has got the right perspective and the right kind of intensity to lead the Indian team,” Kohli said.Kohli was particularly impressed by Gill's clarity when it comes to strategy and his approach to leading the side.“He has got his plans very clear in terms of how he looks at us operating in the field. Of course, with more experience and understanding situations, the kind of calls you take are things that he will keep working on and improving, which everyone does in a leadership role,” he added.Kohli also backed Gill to have a long stint as India's leader“But he has got the desire to lead the Indian cricket team in the right way, which is the most important factor. So, I see him leading for a long time, and he will be absolutely fine,” Kohli said.India will be looking to bounce back from their 1-2 ODI series defeat against England in England in July.India's ODI squad for the West Indies series: Shubman Gill (captain), Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Ruturaj Gaikwad, KL Rahul (vice-captain), Dhruv Jurel, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Ravindra Jadeja, Kuldeep Yadav, Prasidh Krishna, Gurnoor Brar, Mohammed Siraj, Auqib Nabi, Yashasvi Jaiswal and Naman Dhir.Watch the first ODI of West Indies’ tour of India on Sunday, September 27, from 2 PM onwards, LIVE on JioHotstar and Star Sports Network.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Vinod Kambli has shared a message from an elderly care centre in Thane, where he is currently staying, leaving many cricket fans concerned about his health but also reassured by his positive words.The former India cricketer spoke on camera about the care he has been receiving at the Nidan Centre for Elderly Care.He praised the centre’s facilities, especially its hygiene and cleanliness, calling them first class. More importantly, Kambli said the affection shown to him has helped him feel comfortable and at home.“I have received a lot of love,” Kambli said, making it clear that he does not feel far away from home.The video has since circulated on social media, with fans sending their wishes for his health and well-being.Watch:Kambli’s health struggles and cricket journeyKambli has dealt with several health issues in recent years. In December 2024, he was admitted to a hospital in Thane after suffering from low blood pressure and a urinary tract infection. Doctors also found electrolyte imbalances that were affecting his muscles and movement, along with old blood clots in his brain linked to an earlier stroke.He was discharged in January 2025 after spending about two weeks in treatment. Since then, Kambli has made appearances in public, although concerns about his health and mobility have remained.For fans who remember him at his peak, his struggles have been particularly difficult to watch. Kambli was once considered one of India’s most talented batters. He played 17 Tests, scoring 1,084 runs at an average of 54.20, including four centuries. In 104 ODIs, he scored 2,477 runs.His cricket journey is also closely connected to Sachin Tendulkar. articles.title: In 2018, West Indies witnessed Virat Kohli’s 10,000-run record; 8 years later, he chases another unique milestone in ODIs
articles.summary: Virat Kohli is returning to the format that has arguably defined his international career, and the West Indies are one of his favourite opponents.
articles.body: Virat Kohli is returning to the format that has arguably defined his international career, and the West Indies are one of his favourite opponents. As India begin their three-match ODI series against the West Indies on September 27, Kohli carries a staggering record against the Caribbean side - 2,261 runs in 43 matches at an average of 66.50, including nine centuries and 11 fifties. And now, he is just a century awaya to create a unique ODI record.Virat Kohli is one century away to create historyOne of the most significant innings of Kohli's career against West Indies came in Visakhapatnam on October 24, 2018. Kohli smashed an unbeaten 157 off 129 balls, his 37th ODI century. More importantly, the innings took him past the 10,000-run mark in ODI cricket.He reached the landmark in just 205 innings, breaking Sachin Tendulkar's previous record of 259 innings. Kohli became the 13th batter to enter the 10,000-run club but did it considerably faster than anyone before him.Kohli has already scored more ODI centuries against West Indies than any other batter, with nine hundreds to his name. That puts an intriguing milestone in front of him in the upcoming series. Kohli already has 10 ODI centuries against Sri Lanka, and another hundred against West Indies would make him the first batter in ODI history to score 10 centuries against two different teams.It would also extend a remarkable record against an opponent he has consistently dominated across both home and away conditions.157*, 140, 114*: Kohli's memorable knocksKohli's record against West Indies is not simply built on volume. Several of his most memorable ODI performances have come against the Caribbean side.157 off 129, Visakhapatnam, 2018* - This remains Kohli's highest ODI score against West Indies. His unbeaten 157 came with 13 fours and four sixes and also delivered the 10,000-run milestone.140 off 107, Guwahati, 2018 - In the opening ODI of the 2018 series, Kohli produced another spectacular chase. He smashed 140 off 107 balls and shared a 246-run partnership with Rohit Sharma as India chased down 323 with eight wickets in hand.114 off 99, Port of Spain, 2019* - Kohli continued his dominance in the Caribbean in 2019, scoring an unbeaten 114 in a rain-affected ODI at Port of Spain. His century helped India chase down the revised target and complete a 2-0 series win.What makes the West Indies a special opponent for Kohli?Virat Kohli has three Player of the Series awards against West Indies. He scored 453 runs in India's five-match home series against them in 2018, including three centuries, before producing another prolific run in the Caribbean in 2019.Kohli's return to ODI cricket against West Indies therefore comes with more than just another series on the calendar. Also, Virat Kohli is on the verge of making history, needing just 59 runs to reach the monumental milestone of 15,000 ODI runs. Currently standing at 14,941 runs from 314 matches (302 innings), he is set to become only the second batsman in cricket history, after the legendary Sachin Tendulkar, to breach this elite threshold.The first ODI in the three-match series will be played on September 27, giving Kohli his next opportunity to add another chapter to a record that is already extraordinary.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Virat Kohli has revealed that the 2027 ODI World Cup will be his last World Cup for India, with the prospect of one final shot at the coveted
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Virat Kohli has revealed that the 2027 ODI World Cup will be his last World Cup for India, with the prospect of one final shot at the coveted trophy providing the biggest motivation for the batting stalwart.Kohli, who now plays only ODI cricket at the international level, said he is ready to leave everything on the field as India begin their preparations for the 50-over showpiece in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia.Speaking to JioStar ahead of India's ODI series against West Indies, Kohli underlined the unique physical and mental demands of a 50-over World Cup and made it clear that winning the title is his ultimate objective.“The intensity of a 50-over World Cup is greater than anything. Because now, it's about 10 games at a T20 level of intensity. But you are playing 2.5 T20 games in one day. And to maintain that intensity for 10 games in a big tournament and World Cup is a big deal,” Kohli said.“Also now, it's in foreign conditions. It takes a lot out of you. For me, it's the last World Cup I'm going to play for India. And that is my motivation. Like, you know, to leave everything out there. And of course, the goal is absolutely to win the World Cup. And whatever it takes, I'm absolutely ready.”One last World Cup, one clear goalThe 2027 World Cup will give Kohli another opportunity to chase the trophy in what he has now confirmed will be his final ODI World Cup campaign for India.Kohli was part of India's triumphant 2011 World Cup campaign and also played in the 2023 final, where India lost to Australia in Ahmedabad. Across his World Cup career, he has scored 1,795 runs in 37 matches at an average of 59.83, including five centuries and 12 fifties.His overall ODI record stands at 14,941 runs in 302 innings at an average of 58.59, with 54 centuries and 79 fifties.But individual numbers are clearly secondary to Kohli as he looks towards his final World Cup.The 2027 World Cup will be jointly hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia from October 4 to November 21.India's ODI preparations begin with the three-match home series against West Indies, followed by further 50-over assignments as the team builds towards the global tournament.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India batting coach Sitanshu Kotak has backed Yashasvi Jaiswal to continue working hard and wait for his opportunities, insisting that the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India batting coach Sitanshu Kotak has backed Yashasvi Jaiswal to continue working hard and wait for his opportunities, insisting that the young opener’s limited chances in the ODI format should not be viewed as “unfair” treatment.Jaiswal played all three ODIs against Afghanistan at home but was left out of the squad for the subsequent tour of England. The left-hander has, however, returned to the 15-member squad for the three-match ODI series against the West Indies, which begins on Sunday.With Rohit Sharma and captain Shubman Gill likely to remain India’s first-choice opening combination, Jaiswal could once again have to wait for a regular run in the 50-over format.‘He should keep working hard and waiting’Kotak acknowledged the intense competition for places but made it clear that India continue to value Jaiswal.“I think there is so much competition (for team spots) and so many players are performing. Jaiswal…we all know he is one of the best batters and whenever he gets an opportunity he performs. So he is part of the team,” Kotak told reporters on the eve of the first ODI.The batting coach said the support staff were continuing to work with Jaiswal on his game while pointing out that even outstanding players can find themselves waiting when competition for places is fierce.“As a support staff, we look after his skills, practise and his mindset and Gautam (Gambhir) also talks to him a lot, but sometimes you see, say if (for example) there are three very good wicketkeepers, only one can play,” Kotak said.“So, it is not that somebody has been unfair to him. He should keep working hard and waiting for the opportunity and so far whenever he has been getting the opportunity, he has performed,” he added.Jaiswal’s presence in the squad also comes as India begin shaping their plans for the 2027 ODI World Cup in South Africa, with Rohit and Virat Kohli still targeting the global showpiece.Rohit, Kohli bringing ‘experience’ into World Cup build-upKotak believes the presence of senior players can be particularly valuable for youngsters such as Jaiswal as India gradually build towards the World Cup.“See, it is all about selling experience. They always do that. Whenever I have seen all the experienced players, even Gautam because he was playing, the level they have experienced, and when they see some player is going through a similar condition or situation, they always talk to them,” he said.“I think selling experience or selling whatever you have learnt is a great thing to do because it is getting knowledge or refreshing your knowledge as well.”Kotak said India’s planning would be conducted series by series, with the aim of exposing the squad to different conditions before the World Cup.“So from now on, our plan is to do (planning) series by series. Luckily, we have a New Zealand series where it is outside Asia. So, there will be some different conditions - moisture, grass, all will be different,” he said.“If we can successfully do that, within a year's time we should be ready for any challenges, any different wickets or any different bowling attacks,” he added.Jadeja ‘very much in the mix’Ravindra Jadeja’s return to the white-ball squad after an eight-month gap has also added experience to India’s World Cup planning. Kotak said the veteran all-rounder remains firmly in contention.“Jadeja is an outstanding bowler. We all know his records... Jadeja is one of the best fielders on a world level. The experience he has…I actually firmly believe that experience is something you cannot beat,” he said.“Like we see Rohit and Virat, we see Jadeja, they bring a lot to the team,” Kotak added.Kotak also confirmed that Gill is fit for Sunday’s opener after being hit on his right elbow by Mohammed Siraj during training.“Gill is looking good, I think he is good to go tomorrow,” he said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
